That meant Postava, who had never appeared in an NHL game, suddenly found himself protecting Detroit’s lead in Vancouver. Oct 10, 2026; Montreal, Quebec, CAN; Detroit Red Wings goalie John Gibson (36) looks on during warm-up before the game against the Montreal Canadiens at Bell Centre. Mandatory Credit: David Kirouac-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) John Gibson Exits Red Wings Victory With Injury Gibson started Thursday’s game and stopped four of the five shots he faced through the first two periods. Detroit dominated much of the action, including a remarkable second period in which the Canucks failed to register a single shot on goal. However, Gibson did not return to the crease for the final 20 minutes. The Red Wings initially described the issue as an upper-body injury, but head coach Todd McLellan provided additional information afterward. According to the team’s official postgame update , McLellan explained that Gibson was dealing with an issue involving his eye. “He had something in his eye. They’re still looking at it,” McLellan said. The coach also indicated that he learned about the situation late in the second intermission, leaving Detroit little time to prepare for a goaltending change. The extent of Gibson’s injury and his availability for Saturday’s game against Calgary have not yet been determined. Michal Postava Makes Unexpected NHL Debut The timing of Gibson’s departure was particularly unusual because Detroit had already experienced another goaltending injury earlier in the week. As we previously reported following Thursday’s emergency roster moves , the Red Wings recalled Postava from Grand Rapids after Tarasov developed an undisclosed injury. McLellan later explained that Tarasov had aggravated something during Wednesday’s practice, prompting the organization to bring in additional insurance. That decision became extremely important just one day later. Postava entered Thursday’s game at the beginning of the third period and stopped seven of eight shots, helping Detroit preserve its three-goal victory. The 24-year-old had entered the week with an impressive 4-0-0 record, a 1.25 goals-against average, and a .954 save percentage in Grand Rapids. McLellan praised the rookie for responding to a situation neither he nor the coaching staff anticipated. “That’s not the way we planned it,” McLellan acknowledged after the victory. The game’s official scoring recap confirmed that Postava made seven saves in his NHL debut while Lucas Raymond led Detroit offensively with two goals and an assist. Red Wings Face Uncertainty Ahead of Calgary Game The encouraging news is that Tarasov’s injury may not be as serious as initially feared. McLellan described his backup goaltender as day-to-day following Thursday’s game, indicating that Detroit would continue evaluating his condition before making another roster decision. As we previously examined during Detroit’s early-season goaltending debate , Tarasov has been one of the team’s most impressive performers between the pipes. Losing both Gibson and Tarasov for any extended period would place significant pressure on Detroit’s organizational depth, although there has been no indication that either player faces a lengthy absence. For now, Postava provides an intriguing alternative if additional help is needed. The Red Wings improved to 4-3-3 with Thursday’s victory and have collected points in six consecutive games. Their next challenge comes Saturday night against the Calgary Flames, followed by a Monday matchup with the Edmonton Oilers. Detroit’s recent momentum is encouraging, but its goaltending situation has suddenly become one of the biggest questions surrounding the team. What began as a precautionary emergency recall Thursday morning turned into an unexpected NHL debut that evening. Now the Red Wings must determine whether their regular goaltenders will be healthy enough to finish the road trip.

item.title: WWE Rumor Claims Sin Cara Character Could Return: 8 Current Stars Who Could Don the Mask, Including Axiom
item.description: WWE Over the last couple of years, WWE has made an effort to increase its Spanish-speaking fan base. Stars like Penta and Stephanie Vaquer are just a couple of the Latin performers featured each week on episodes of RAW and SmackDown. Furthermore, before WrestleMania 41 last year, the company purchased legendary Mexican promotion AAA and has a lot of crossover between it and its established brands. Now, according to PW Insider, there has been a recent push backstage to bring back the character Sin Cara . Mexican star Mistico was under the mask when the character debuted in 2011. Then, when he had creative differences with management, he was replaced by Hunico. The character never really took off with fans, but it is still owned by WWE and can be used by any performer. If WWE does decide to bring the character back, we take a look at seven stars who could be the next Sin Cara. Joaquin Wilde & Cruz del Toro As a tag team, Cruz Del Toro and Joaquin Wilde have showcased some impressive athleticism and skill. However, during stints in Legado del Fantasma and the LWO, they never built a fanbase. Both are still under contract with the company because WWE clearly sees value in them and has used their talents in AAA. If Sin Cars returns, it would not be a surprise if either man were under the mask. Romeo Moreno NXT star Romeo Moreno is an exciting young talent with potential. The company could continue his development on the black and gold brand over the next couple of years. However, on a pure athleticism level, he would be a good fit to be the new Sin Cara. And because he is only 24, he could work under the mask for the next two decades. Axiom & Nathan Frazer A case can be made that Fraxiom is the best tag team on any brand in WWE. However, promoting their tag division continues to be a weakness for the company. So it means that both Axiom and Nathan Frazer will always be in danger of being in the next round of roster cuts unless the company gives them a serious long-term creative push. If that push doesn’t come — and it really should — either man would make a ton of sense as the new Sin Cara. While the assumption would be that that character would be a native of Mexico, the Spanish and English stars’ skill sets are a great fit for the character. Kale Dixon Development talent Kale Dixon has been off NXT TV for months due to a rumored injury and after his tag team with Uriah Connors was dissolved. While he is bigger than the two men who previously donned the mantle, he has a ton of athletic talent, is young, and is in creative limbo. Returning to the ring as a very different version of the character makes some sense. It would make sense to bring him back as the character fans previously saw to give French wrestling fans a favorite star. item.title: Colts QB Anthony Richardson Sr. reportedly charged with marijuana possession
item.description: KANSAS CITY, MO - Anthony Richardson Sr.of the Indianapolis Colts before an NFL game between the Indianapolis Colts and Kansas City Chiefs. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Anthony Richardson Sr. of the Indianapolis Colts is facing a misdemeanor charge for possession of marijuana following an Oct. 12 traffic stop in Carmel, Indiana, according to FOX59 . “We are aware of the situation involving Anthony Richardson and are currently gathering additional information,” the Colts said in a statement. “We will have no further comment at this time.” Court documents obtained by FOX59/CBS4 show that charges were filed on Monday, a week after police officers stopped Richardson's black 2023 Dodge Charger. The vehicle's registration was reportedly expired and was assigned to a different car. According to police, the car pulled over to the side of the road and officers noticed the "odor of marijuana" as they approached. Richardson reportedly admitted that he did smoke marijuana in the car so as to not do so in front of his children. He also told police that he possessed a small amount of marijuana in the car. The quarterback was handcuffed after exiting the car and officers proceeded with searching the vehicle. A small mason jar was reportedly found containing a substance believed to be marijuana and a bag of THC-infused gummies that was opened. The substance reportedly tested positive for THC. Richardson was also cited for the expired registration. A hearing was scheduled for Dec. 9, but has since been waived. A bench trial will be held on Jan. 2027. Richardson is the second Colts player to have a run-in with police this season. Wide receiver Keenan Allen was charged with two misdemeanors following his August arrest on suspicion of driving under the influence.

item.title: Giants don’t back down from ‘traitors’ message. ‘There’s no excuse for it’
item.description: Dennard Wilson didn’t name names. He didn’t need to. The Giants ’ first-year defensive coordinator on Thursday publicly blasted the effort of some of his players , two days after he did the same behind closed doors. Later Thursday, in the locker room, those players embraced the criticism as they prepared for this weekend’s trip to Houston, where the Giants need their defense to carry them in quarterback J.J. McCarthy’s first start. They all know this: If they don’t fix the effort problems that emerged in last Sunday’s loss to the Saints, they won’t win the NFC East, even in a down year for the division. “I totally agree with him,” slot cornerback Dru Phillips said of Wilson’s criticism. “You watch some of that tape, and you’re like, ‘That’s bulls---.’ We know that we’re better. We took it to heart, as in: Let’s do it — and we’re going to be better at it.” Phillips was one of the players who loafed against the Saints. So Wilson’s words this week felt uncomfortable for him. “It’s supposed to be uncomfortable,” he said. “You’re supposed to feel that pressure. We all felt it, and it’s like: We better fix it. It’s an embarrassing moment when you’re not running to the ball in this game. You can’t do that.” Wilson didn’t like the downfield pursuit and tackling energy on a few plays against the Saints. item.content:encoded: Dennard Wilson didn’t name names. He didn’t need to. The Giants ’ first-year defensive coordinator on Thursday publicly blasted the effort of some of his players , two days after he did the same behind closed doors. Later Thursday, in the locker room, those players embraced the criticism as they prepared for this weekend’s trip to Houston, where the Giants need their defense to carry them in quarterback J.J. McCarthy’s first start. They all know this: If they don’t fix the effort problems that emerged in last Sunday’s loss to the Saints, they won’t win the NFC East, even in a down year for the division. “I totally agree with him,” slot cornerback Dru Phillips said of Wilson’s criticism. “You watch some of that tape, and you’re like, ‘That’s bulls---.’ We know that we’re better. We took it to heart, as in: Let’s do it — and we’re going to be better at it.” Phillips was one of the players who loafed against the Saints. So Wilson’s words this week felt uncomfortable for him. “It’s supposed to be uncomfortable,” he said. “You’re supposed to feel that pressure. We all felt it, and it’s like: We better fix it. It’s an embarrassing moment when you’re not running to the ball in this game. You can’t do that.” Wilson didn’t like the downfield pursuit and tackling energy on a few plays against the Saints. The most notable was Alvin Kamara’s 31-yard catch-and-run touchdown that broke a 10-10 tie early in the third quarter. Safety Jason Pinnock whiffed on the initial tackle, though he didn’t loaf. Several of his teammates clearly did — Jevon Holland, Tremaine Edmunds, Phillips and Jihad Ward (who has since been released). Holland is in the concussion protocol, so he is not permitted to speak with reporters. Edmunds and Phillips did address the play on Thursday after Wilson’s fiery press conference. Edmunds — who might be out a while with a shoulder injury — mostly dodged questions about his effort. Phillips did not. Phillips said he expected Pinnock to make the initial tackle, which he noted is “the wrong thing [to do] in football.” Phillips specifically said he did not run hard enough to the ball. On the sideline after the touchdown, the Giants’ defenders told each other: “Guys, we’ve got to hustle.” So they knew immediately that they had screwed up. Giants defensive back Dru Phillis (No. 22) was among many defensive players called out by defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson for their effort in the loss to the Saints. AP Photo/Frank Franklin II “It’s embarrassing, because you have 10 other guys depending on you,” Phillips said of his lackluster effort. “When you’re not giving that hustle that you should be, you feel like: ‘I let everybody down.’ There’s no excuse for it. I’ve got to hustle.” Meanwhile, Edmunds — the Giants’ ninth-year middle linebacker — deflected a question about what he could have done differently on Kamara’s touchdown. “We’re not pointing the finger,” he said. “I’m pretty sure we all have some plays that we wish we had back.” Still, he said the Giants’ defensive players fully heard and understood Wilson’s message. “It’s not just his message,” Edmunds said. “It’s our message to each other: What do we want our defense to look like? Because at the end of the day, it’s our defense as players.” During Tuesday’s defensive meeting, Wilson spotlighted the plays he didn’t like from the Saints game — while directly (and apparently profanely) calling players out by name, including Phillips. None of the Giants’ players spoke in that meeting. They just listened to Wilson’s angry message and absorbed his critiques. When Wilson met with reporters on Thursday, he vented about his players’ poor effort, putting his frustration out in the open — something his predecessor, Shane Bowen, never really did. “Last week was one of our worst tackling games,” Wilson said. “I wasn’t happy with our effort running to the ball. We put some stuff on tape that was not characteristic of a New York Giant defense. It’s unacceptable, and it will be changed.” Wilson said he shows those lackluster plays and makes a point of calling out players directly — in the defensive and full team meeting — for a reason. “We confront everything,” he said. “I look at guys that don’t run to the ball, and I call them traitors, because they’re traitors to the defense. When you have a traitor to the defense, you either have to make adjustments to get them off the field or they have to correct their behaviors. “Last week, we did not on every play run to the ball, and it was unacceptable. The guys know it. If your effort is bad, if you have a lack of toughness, it gets pointed out. When you have behaviors that are unacceptable, we’re not going to accept it. And if you don’t change the behaviors, we have to change the players.” The Giants’ defenders are not surprised by how directly Wilson has handled this situation. It is typical of his direct coaching personality. “Any time you try to be a dynamic defense, honesty is the best policy,” Edmunds said. Safety Tyler Nubin — who missed the Saints game with a neck injury — said players appreciate how Wilson takes things head-on, while striking an ideal balance between praise and criticism. “He’s going to shoot you straight,” Nubin told NJ.com. “He’s not going to sugarcoat anything. He’s going to tell you what you’re doing well, as well. He’s just real. That’s what you want out of a coach. “You want somebody to be honest with you. You don’t want somebody to be blowing smoke up your ass all the time. And you don’t want somebody motherf---ing you and only talking about the things that you did wrong. “There’s no gray area [with Wilson]. Sometimes, some coaches can give you a little gray area. Some coaches like to cover their own ass, but he doesn’t do that. He doesn’t really care about the outside noise.” Nubin acknowledged the obvious: Wilson’s approach is “definitely” a change from Bowen, who arrived in East Rutherford alongside Nubin in 2024. “I’d say he’s a lot more direct,” Nubin said of Wilson. “He’s not going to wait and pull you to the side. He’s going to tell you in front of the whole entire unit. Having that honesty with everybody, it just makes everybody want to play better for each other.” Last season, when Bowen was fired in November, it became obvious that his less-than-direct approach was the wrong one for these Giants. How will Wilson’s style play out over the long haul? For now, Pinnock — a sixth-year safety — said the Giants’ players left his meeting with resolve. “That was probably the best tough meeting to have,” he told NJ.com. “I’ve been in those type of situations where it’s just straight finger pointing [from the coach]. And you walk out, and everybody has their side remarks, like: ‘Ah, man, whatever.’ Nah, that was positive, and it was needed. It’s not like somebody feels targeted.” Pinnock said this stems from the tight relationships Wilson, 44, has built with his players. “It’s going to feel personal if I don’t know you,” Pinnock said. “Dennard, he talks to all of us on and off the field, jokes with us, learns our humor. He knows his personnel, so he knows how to get the best out of everybody. I think it was a good meeting.” So how does Pinnock think the Giants’ defense will respond in Houston? “How we should: Go get a W,” he said. McCarthy starting quarterback Giants are rolling the dice with big change on offense: ‘You never know. It might work’ Read the original article on NJ.com . item.title: Kovac praises Schlotterbeck's commitment
item.description: Kovac praises Schlotterbeck's commitment All the players who made the trip came through the match in Baku unscathed. “Yesterday was a day off from training. That was very important after all the kilometres we had to cover,” says BVB coach Niko Kovac. Konstantinos Karetsas had already missed out in midweek due to a ligament injury in his foot and will also be unavailable against Eintracht. Kovac could not yet say whether he would be an option for Tuesday’s cup match against Bremen. Kaua Prates has a minor muscle problem. Justin Lerma remains sidelined with a more serious muscle injury. Nico Schlotterbeck returned early from international duty with an ankle injury but was back on the pitch straight after the international break. He only sat out the match against Bodø/Glimt to manage his workload. Speaking about the centre-back, Kovac says: “He has pain in his ankle from time to time. It can’t possibly have healed 100 per cent yet. But you can see how important he is to the team and how he gives everything for them. Every single game gives him the chance to improve his fitness.” (cr) This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇩🇪 here.

item.title: Gasperini’s Faith in Emanuele Lulli Pays Off as Roma Pursue New Deal
item.description: ROME, ITALY - OCTOBER 17: Emanuele Lulli of Roma celebrates his goal during the Serie A match between AS Roma and Genoa CFC at Stadio Olimpico on October 17, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Image Photo Agency/Getty Images) | Getty Images While we all hope Roma’s return to the Champions League will usher in a new era of free-wheeling spending on the transfer market, sustained success still requires significant building from within. Homegrown players are not only more cost-effective, but they also bring what we might call corporate knowledge: insight and investment in the club’s values. These combined factors foster a sense of identity and camaraderie, while freeing up funds to acquire the finishing pieces the club needs to achieve its long-range goals. We’ve seen this approach work over the years with players as varied as Francesco Totti and Alessandro Florenzi, while talents like Niccolò Pisilli will ensure that Roma’s identity remains intact. And thanks to his breakout campaign, we can now add Emmanuele Lulli to that list. The 19-year-old wing-back just missed the cut in this summer’s U-23 countdown, but Lulli has been a hot name on prospect radars for the past couple of seasons. All Lulli needed was a manager willing to give him a chance to learn and grow on the job, one willing to ride the highs and lows that come with relying on teenage talents. Enter Gian Piero Gasperini. Never one to shy away from relying on unproven players, Gasperini has thrown Lulli into the deep end this season, and Roma is reaping the rewards. With five appearances, including four starts in Roma’s first seven league matches, Lulli is flourishing under Gasperini’s tutelage, flashing an impressive blend of attacking prowess and defensive acumen. Lulli reached his early-season peak last weekend, scoring his first professional goal in the Giallorossi’s 2-0 win at the Olimpico against Genoa. The 19-year-old Roman’s future is looking brighter by the day, so much so that the club is already making moves to ensure he remains in their warm embrace. Accordo trovato tra l' #ASRoma ed Emanuele #Lulli per il rinnovo di contratto. I giallorossi blindano il giovane che era in scadenza di contratto (dopo @Dani1998Aloisi ) @tempoweb pic.twitter.com/Q4oAgcYPXI — Filippo Biafora (@Fil_Biafora) October 23, 2026 According to multiple Italian sources, Roma and Lulli’s reps are working on a new contract that will keep the Roman boy at the Olimpico for the foreseeable future. While nothing is official yet, rumors suggest Lulli will sign a new deal through 2031, ensuring his best days (if not his entire career) are spent in giallo e rosso.

item.title: How to get and use fulton drop markers in DMZ in Modern Warfare 4
item.description: Fulton drop markers in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's DMZ mode are essentially portable exfil points. They're categorized as ultra loot though, which is the rarest tier in the game, making them extremely hard to get your hands on. Some players have them early, however, thanks to the deluxe edition of the game granting them via a survival starter kit.
item.dc:creator: Ford James

item.title: Vikings’ Jauan Jennings Has New Potential Trade Landing Spot
item.description: The Minnesota Vikings could trade wide receiver Jauan Jennings despite being 5-0 to begin this season. Getty The Minnesota Vikings could trade wide receiver Jauan Jennings despite being 5-0 to begin this season. Getty The Minnesota Vikings could send Jauan Jennings to the Washington Commanders to give quarterback Jayden Daniels another pass target. Getty There has been no shortage of suggested trade destinations for Minnesota Vikings receiver Jauan Jennings. Another one, though, has seemingly emerged this week. Heavy Sports proposes the Vikings trade Jennings to the Washington Commanders in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round draft pick. The Vikings signed Jennings to a 1-year, $8 million deal over the offseason. Pundits expected the veteran to supply much-needed depth for Minnesota as a WR3. But Jennings has received just five targets in four games this season. He has caught two of those targets for nine yards. Why Vikings Could Part With WR Jauan Jennings at NFL Trade Deadline Getty The Minnesota Vikings could trade wide receiver Jauan Jennings despite being 5-0 to begin this season. Jennings just simply isn’t working out for the Vikings this season. He’s barely involved in the offense. Over the past two weeks, Myles Price has started receiving more targets than the veteran. That makes Jennings a trade candidate even though the Vikings are contending. Enough teams have a need at receiver that Jennings could be in demand. With a Jennings trade, Minnesota could basically buy a draft pick. Meaning, the financial investment the team made in Jennings for the first half of this season will give the team an extra Day 3 selection. If the Vikings deal Jennings, the team could move forward with Price and Tai Felton as their options behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison . What Jennings Could Bring to Commanders Getty The Minnesota Vikings could send Jauan Jennings to the Washington Commanders to give quarterback Jayden Daniels another pass target. Jennings is a potential trade target for the Commanders because the team just lost veteran starting receiver Terry McLaurin for the rest of the season. McLaurin suffered a torn patellar tendon on Monday night. Teams don’t typically make trades within the same conference. But the Vikings might not have an issue with that since it doesn’t appear likely they will compete with the Commanders for a playoff spot. Washington is 1-4-1 entering this week while Minnesota sits at 5-0. The Commanders could see Jennings as a short-term McLaurin replacement. Jennings could finish the season with Washington and potentially be a lot more productive than he has been in Minnesota. Last season, Jennings posted 55 catches, 643 receiving yards and a career-best nine touchdowns. Jennings reached new heights with 77 catches and 975 receiving yards during 2024. In Washington, the veteran could start opposite Stefon Diggs for the remainder of 2026. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Vikings’ Jauan Jennings Has New

item.title: LIVE! UFC 333 Ceremonial Weigh Ins Video!
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 24: Alexander Volkanovski of Australia poses on the scale during the UFC 266 ceremonial weigh-in at Park Theater on September 24, 2021 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Zuffa LLC) With the UFC 333 early (and official) weigh ins already in the books ( get full results and video here ), the cast and crew of tomorrow’s (Sat., Oct. 24, 2026) “Volkanovski vs. Evloev” mixed martial arts (MMA) event on Paramount+ will head to Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi, UAE, for the ceremonial weigh ins and corresponding festivities, streaming LIVE at 10 a.m. ET (7 a.m. PT) in the embedded video above. UFC 333 features the featherweight title fight between current 145-pound champion Alexander Volkanovski and undefeated division contender Movsar Evloev . In the UFC 333 co-main event, Petr Yan defends his bantamweight strap opposite former 135-pound titleholder Merab Dvalishvili . “This preparation is different just because I pushed more than ever,” Evloev said . “And we did more of everything to make sure we didn’t miss anything. He hasn’t beaten anyone like me. There’s many things that make me special, like unique. And I’m about to show it Saturday.” Additional main card matchups include the flyweight fracas pitting Lone’er Kavanagh against Ramazan Temirov, while Alexander Volkov and Rizvan Kuniev hook ‘em up at 265 pounds. In addition, Aaron Pico collides with Losene Keita in featherweight action. For the rest of the UFC 333 fight card and Paramount+ lineup click here .

item.title: Kovac counts on fans against Frankfurt: „Roar us to victory“
item.description: Kovac counts on fans against Frankfurt: „Roar us to victory“ The situation After the “three Bs” of Bodø, Berlin and Baku, involving more than 11,000 kilometres of travel , Borussia Dortmund return to their home ground, SIGNAL IDUNA PARK, for the first time in two weeks to face Eintracht Frankfurt. “We’re finally playing at home again. It’s good to play in front of your own fans. I hope they’ll roar us on to victory,” says BVB coach Niko Kovac ahead of the match. Back at their own stadium, BVB are looking to return to winning ways in the Bundesliga. Four wins at the start of the season were followed by two draws: 2-2 against Bremen and 0-0 away to Union Berlin. Sharing the points in the capital saw BVB drop to second in the table – albeit only on goal difference. Like the Black & Yellows, league leaders Bayern Munich have 14 points. A win would put Dortmund top for at least one night, with the record champions not in action until Sunday in Freiburg. A key foundation for that is the best defence in the league so far: BVB have conceded just four goals and have already kept four clean sheets. Team news All the players who travelled to Baku came through the match unscathed. “Yesterday was a day off from training. That was very important after all the kilometres we’d had to cover,” says Kovac. Find out here who will miss the Frankfurt match and who received special praise from the coach. The opposition Frankfurt recently celebrated their first home win of the season, beating 1. FC Köln 1-0. Before that, Eintracht had lost 6-0 away in Leipzig. With two wins, two draws and two defeats, the Hesse club sit 11th. They have already conceded 16 goals in six Bundesliga matches – four times as many as BVB. Against Köln, Frankfurt kept their first clean sheet of the season. “They would certainly like to have a few more points, but their performances in recent matches have been inconsistent. A draw, a defeat, a win – there’s been a bit of everything,” says Kovac. “They’re a team that will be in the top third of the table at the end of the season. I’m convinced of that.” The Bundesliga head-to-head record against Eintracht favours BVB: the Black & Yellows have beaten Frankfurt more often than any other club – 52 times in total. Dortmund have won 14 of their last 15 home matches against the Hesse side. Another Dortmund victory would also mark Eintracht’s 500th away defeat in the Bundesliga. The coaches On Saturday, Niko Kovac will face an old acquaintance on the touchline: Adi Hütter. The two coaches have met seven times so far – the first time 17 years ago, in October 2009, when Kovac’s Salzburg Juniors faced Hütter’s SCR Altach. They have also worked at some of the same clubs: Hütter succeeded the current BVB coach in Frankfurt in 2018, and both later coached AS Monaco. Today, Kovac’s focus is on the Black & Yellows: “Wherever I work, I always put my heart into it,” says the BVB coach. “We want to lift some silverware too. We have to work hard for that, and we’ll

Against Köln, Frankfurt kept their first clean sheet of the season. “They would certainly like to have a few more points, but their performances in recent matches have been inconsistent. A draw, a defeat, a win – there’s been a bit of everything,” says Kovac. “They’re a team that will be in the top third of the table at the end of the season. I’m convinced of that.” The Bundesliga head-to-head record against Eintracht favours BVB: the Black & Yellows have beaten Frankfurt more often than any other club – 52 times in total. Dortmund have won 14 of their last 15 home matches against the Hesse side. Another Dortmund victory would also mark Eintracht’s 500th away defeat in the Bundesliga. The coaches On Saturday, Niko Kovac will face an old acquaintance on the touchline: Adi Hütter. The two coaches have met seven times so far – the first time 17 years ago, in October 2009, when Kovac’s Salzburg Juniors faced Hütter’s SCR Altach. They have also worked at some of the same clubs: Hütter succeeded the current BVB coach in Frankfurt in 2018, and both later coached AS Monaco. Today, Kovac’s focus is on the Black & Yellows: “Wherever I work, I always put my heart into it,” says the BVB coach. “We want to lift some silverware too. We have to work hard for that, and we’ll give it everything we’ve got.” Christina Reinke This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. item.title: Lewandowski backs Lamine Yamal to win the 2026 Ballon d’Or: ‘He’s incredible, especially for his age’
item.description: Lewandowski backs Lamine Yamal to win the 2026 Ballon d’Or: ‘He’s incredible, especially for his age’ Robert Lewandowski wants Lamine Yamal to win the 2026 Ballon d’Or, but the former Barcelona striker also highlighted Bayern Munich duo Michael Olise and Harry Kane as serious contenders for football’s most prestigious individual award. Speaking to The Athletic (h/t Mundo Deportivo ) ahead of Monday’s ceremony , Lewandowski praised Yamal’s extraordinary ability at such a young age while suggesting the race is more open than during the era dominated by Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo. Lewandowski explains why the Ballon d’Or race is more open For much of the past two decades, the Ballon d’Or was largely a contest between Messi and Ronaldo. The pair collected 13 awards between 2008 and 2023, with Luka Modric in 2018 and Karim Benzema in 2022 the only players to interrupt their dominance during that period. Lewandowski believes the current landscape offers a wider range of potential winners. “We come from an era where two or three players were the clear favorites to win the Ballon d’Or. Now I see that it’s a bit more open. Perhaps you can assess 10 players and find that they all have a case for winning this Ballon d’Or,” explained the Polish striker Lewandowski wants Lamine to win the Ballon d’Or. (Photo by Eric Alonso/Getty Images) Although Lewandowski is no longer in contention himself, having moved to MLS with Chicago Fire after his Barcelona spell, he remains closely interested in the race. He singled out Lamine, whom he watched develop from his debut for Barcelona at just 15, as one of the players he would most like to see lift the trophy. “Of course, I wish Lamine Yamal wins the Ballon d’Or, because he is incredible, especially for his age, but even so, if you compare him to the previous era, he’s a bit different,” Lewandowski said. Michael Olise earns special praise alongside Harry Kane Lewandowski did not limit his assessment to his former Barcelona teammate. The veteran striker also highlighted Bayern Munich’s attacking partnership between Kane, Olise and Luis Diaz, describing their combination as an excellent fit. “Harry Kane arrived at Bayern at the peak of his powers, and what he is doing is incredible, the number of goals he scores. Bayern had been missing a striker of that calibre after I left,” Lewandowski said. He also praised Olise’s ability to influence matches, pointing to the winger’s decision-making in front of goal and his understanding of when to shoot or create an opportunity for a teammate. Kane and Olise also in the running. Speaking to The Athletic (h/t Mundo Deportivo ) ahead of Monday’s ceremony , Lewandowski praised Yamal’s extraordinary ability at such a young age while suggesting the race is more open than during the era dominated by Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo. Lewandowski explains why the Ballon d’Or race is more open For much of the past two decades, the Ballon d’Or was largely a contest between Messi and Ronaldo. The pair collected 13 awards between 2008 and 2023, with Luka Modric in 2018 and Karim Benzema in 2022 the only players to interrupt their dominance during that period. Lewandowski believes the current landscape offers a wider range of potential winners. “We come from an era where two or three players were the clear favorites to win the Ballon d’Or. Now I see that it’s a bit more open. Perhaps you can assess 10 players and find that they all have a case for winning this Ballon d’Or,” explained the Polish striker Lewandowski wants Lamine to win the Ballon d’Or. (Photo by Eric Alonso/Getty Images) Although Lewandowski is no longer in contention himself, having moved to MLS with Chicago Fire after his Barcelona spell, he remains closely interested in the race. He singled out Lamine, whom he watched develop from his debut for Barcelona at just 15, as one of the players he would most like to see lift the trophy. “Of course, I wish Lamine Yamal wins the Ballon d’Or, because he is incredible, especially for his age, but even so, if you compare him to the previous era, he’s a bit different,” Lewandowski said. Michael Olise earns special praise alongside Harry Kane Lewandowski did not limit his assessment to his former Barcelona teammate. The veteran striker also highlighted Bayern Munich’s attacking partnership between Kane, Olise and Luis Diaz, describing their combination as an excellent fit. “Harry Kane arrived at Bayern at the peak of his powers, and what he is doing is incredible, the number of goals he scores. Bayern had been missing a striker of that calibre after I left,” Lewandowski said. He also praised Olise’s ability to influence matches, pointing to the winger’s decision-making in front of goal and his understanding of when to shoot or create an opportunity for a teammate. Kane and Olise also in the running. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) When comparing Olise with Yamal, Lewandowski acknowledged that the Barcelona youngster receives much of the attention but argued that the Bayern winger deserves equal consideration. “Lamine and Olise, as wingers, are among the most powerful players in their team, alongside Harry Kane as a striker. I am impressed by the type of player Olise is. He has a huge future ahead of him,” he said. Lewandowski went further by suggesting that a stronger World Cup scoring record could have transformed Olise’s standing in the Ballon d’Or race. “For me, probably if Olise had scored one or two goals at the World Cup, he would be the favourite to win the Ballon d’Or, alongside Lamine Yamal or Harry Kane,” he added. Lewandowski’s endorsement of Yamal is unsurprising given their time together at Barcelona. At the same time, though, his comments on Kane and Olise suggest that the race for the top honour remains tightly contested.

item.title: Raiders news: Andrew Janocko sees Michael Mayer as valuable piece
item.description: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are preparing for their matchup with the Los Angeles Rams. It will be their chance to end a three-game losing streak after starting 3-0. Michael Mayer will look to duplicate his Week 6 performance. He had a career game last week for the Silver and Black. 95 receiving yards was his highest total since being drafted into the NFL. He has become a vital piece in the passing game. The Raiders coaching staff is not surprised. Offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko spoke of his value to the team during his press conference on Thursday. “Yeah, Mike [Mayer] is a valuable piece to this team because of the person that Mike is, starting with that. So, you start with an ultimate competitor. You start with somebody that comes to work each and every single day, and then you take the football skill set and how he has developed as a player, how he’s developing in a leadership role. He’s going to be a part of our success going forward.” His stats this season were expected. Janocko loves his work and study habits as Mayer is in the front row during team meetings. “I think you just watch Mike [Mayer work every single day in everything he does, run game, pass game protections, and how he takes nothing lightly. Watching Mike, Mike sits in the front row of the meeting rooms and just watching him take note and how he pays attention, and then it applies on the field. It’s just that’s what you look for in a consummate pro.“ Raider Nation should expect Mayer to keep producing in this offense. If teams try to take away Bowers, Mayer’s production will keep rising. In other Raiders links: Mike Washington Jr. did not practice Thursday : Washington Jr. was designated DNP on Thursday’s injury report, raising concerns he could miss Sunday. The Raiders are struggling in the second half of games : Ryan McFadden deep dives into why the Raiders are struggling in the second half this season. Puka Nacua leaves practice early: The Rams are dealing with a ton of injuries, and now Puka Nacua left practice with a calf injury.

item.title: Today in Motorsport History, October 23: MotoGP Lost Marco Simoncelli at Sepang in 2011
item.description: A pack of riders leans through a corner. Illustrative image, not from the 2011 Malaysian Grand Prix. Photo: Harvey Tan Villarino / Pexels Marco Simoncelli died at Sepang 15 years ago today, on October 23, 2011, after a crash on the second lap of the Malaysian Grand Prix. He was 24. The race was red-flagged, a restart was pencilled in and then dropped, and one lap was all MotoGP got. No winner was declared and no points were awarded. It was the first death in the premier class since Daijiro Kato’s at the 2003 Japanese Grand Prix, and it came just over a year after Moto2 rider Shoya Tomizawa died at Misano. The season he was finally having Simoncelli arrived in 2011 as the 2008 250cc world champion, in his second year with the San Carlo Honda Gresini team after finishing eighth in the 2010 standings. This was the year it came together. He took pole at Catalunya in June, stood on the podium at Brno, and a week before Sepang finished second to Casey Stoner at Phillip Island, his best result in the class. He was sixth in the championship, he had signed to stay with Gresini for 2012 on a Honda RC213V, and he was the satellite rider who could actually run with the factory bikes. Phillip Island, for what it is worth, would produce a very different kind of Sunday two years later, which we covered in our Márquez black-flag story . It had also been a heavy week for the sport. Dan Wheldon was killed in the IndyCar finale at Las Vegas on October 16, the same day Stoner clinched his second MotoGP title in Australia. Paddocks do not recover from a week like that, and Sepang was the next stop. Sunday at Sepang Fact Detail Date Sunday, October 23, 2011 Event Malaysian Grand Prix, round 17 of the 2011 MotoGP season Circuit Sepang International Circuit, Malaysia (5.543 km) MotoGP pole Dani Pedrosa, Repsol Honda (2:01.462) Crash Lap 2, exit of Turn 11 Riders involved Marco Simoncelli, Colin Edwards, Valentino Rossi Declared dead 4:56pm local time Race result Abandoned after one lap; no winner, no points awarded 2011 Malaysian Grand Prix, MotoGP class. Sources: Sepang International Circuit statement, October 25, 2011; MotoGP race records. Pedrosa took pole with a Repsol Honda lockout of the front row, and Stoner took the lead from Pedrosa and Andrea Dovizioso at the start. On lap two, Simoncelli, running fourth, lost the front end on the exit of the Turn 11 right-hander. Bike and rider slid across the track and into the path of Colin Edwards (Tech 3 Yamaha) and Valentino Rossi (Ducati), who had no room to avoid him. Both hit him. Edwards suffered a separated shoulder, and Rossi got his bike back to the pits. Simoncelli’s helmet came off in the impact. Two riders trade lines through a corner. Illustrative image, not from the 2011 Malaysian Grand Prix. Photo: Cipriano Fernandes / Pexels The race was red-flagged immediately. MotoGP medical director Michele Macchiagodena said Simoncelli went into cardiac arrest in the ambulance, and doctors worked on him for about 45 min
item.content:encoded: A pack of riders leans through a corner. Illustrative image, not from the 2011 Malaysian Grand Prix. Photo: Harvey Tan Villarino / Pexels Marco Simoncelli died at Sepang 15 years ago today, on October 23, 2011, after a crash on the second lap of the Malaysian Grand Prix. He was 24. The race was red-flagged, a restart was pencilled in and then dropped, and one lap was all MotoGP got. No winner was declared and no points were awarded. It was the first death in the premier class since Daijiro Kato’s at the 2003 Japanese Grand Prix, and it came just over a year after Moto2 rider Shoya Tomizawa died at Misano. The season he was finally having Simoncelli arrived in 2011 as the 2008 250cc world champion, in his second year with the San Carlo Honda Gresini team after finishing eighth in the 2010 standings. This was the year it came together. He took pole at Catalunya in June, stood on the podium at Brno, and a week before Sepang finished second to Casey Stoner at Phillip Island, his best result in the class. He was sixth in the championship, he had signed to stay with Gresini for 2012 on a Honda RC213V, and he was the satellite rider who could actually run with the factory bikes. Phillip Island, for what it is worth, would produce a very different kind of Sunday two years later, which we covered in our Márquez black-flag story . It had also been a heavy week for the sport. Dan Wheldon was killed in the IndyCar finale at Las Vegas on October 16, the same day Stoner clinched his second MotoGP title in Australia. Paddocks do not recover from a week like that, and Sepang was the next stop. Sunday at Sepang Fact Detail Date Sunday, October 23, 2011 Event Malaysian Grand Prix, round 17 of the 2011 MotoGP season Circuit Sepang International Circuit, Malaysia (5.543 km) MotoGP pole Dani Pedrosa, Repsol Honda (2:01.462) Crash Lap 2, exit of Turn 11 Riders involved Marco Simoncelli, Colin Edwards, Valentino Rossi Declared dead 4:56pm local time Race result Abandoned after one lap; no winner, no points awarded 2011 Malaysian Grand Prix, MotoGP class. Sources: Sepang International Circuit statement, October 25, 2011; MotoGP race records. Pedrosa took pole with a Repsol Honda lockout of the front row, and Stoner took the lead from Pedrosa and Andrea Dovizioso at the start. On lap two, Simoncelli, running fourth, lost the front end on the exit of the Turn 11 right-hander. Bike and rider slid across the track and into the path of Colin Edwards (Tech 3 Yamaha) and Valentino Rossi (Ducati), who had no room to avoid him. Both hit him. Edwards suffered a separated shoulder, and Rossi got his bike back to the pits. Simoncelli’s helmet came off in the impact. Two riders trade lines through a corner. Illustrative image, not from the 2011 Malaysian Grand Prix. Photo: Cipriano Fernandes / Pexels The race was red-flagged immediately. MotoGP medical director Michele Macchiagodena said Simoncelli went into cardiac arrest in the ambulance, and doctors worked on him for about 45 minutes before declaring him dead at 4:56pm local time. A 4:30pm restart had been planned, then delayed, then cancelled. Sepang’s chairman said two days later that the circuit and Dorna had agreed the race could not continue, and that the circuit had followed every precaution required by the FIM, the Malaysian motorsport authority and Dorna. Stoner, who had taken the lead at the start, said watching the footage left him feeling “sick inside.” Why it mattered Two deaths in just over a year, in two different classes, changed the tone of the paddock. Simoncelli was one of the most popular riders in it, and “Super Sic” was the name on his team’s own tribute that night. The crash itself began as an ordinary front-end slide at a corner exit, the kind of fall riders walk away from most weekends. That is what made it so hard for the sport to absorb. It also sharpened a question that never fully went away: how much protection a helmet can promise when everything goes wrong at once. Simoncelli’s helmet separated from his head in the impact, and the helmet’s developer later attributed that to the chin strap tearing out. That discussion has not stopped. For a current example of how differently racing’s rulebooks treat helmet life, see our look at the helmet that expires differently in every rulebook . A rider leans a bike through a corner. Illustrative image, not from Sepang. Photo: Harvey Tan Villarino / Pexels What changed, and what didn’t Be careful with the word “changed.” In the sources I could verify, the crash is not tied to a single rule rewrite. Sepang’s own statement said the circuit would work with the FIM and Dorna on whether further rider-safety measures were possible, and that is as specific as the official record gets. What did change is easier to see and name: Misano’s circuit was renamed Misano World Circuit Marco Simoncelli, announced in November 2011 and made official the following year. The Fondazione Marco Simoncelli 58 was set up in his name, and his father Paolo later started the Sic58 Squadra Corse team. On September 8, 2016, ahead of the San Marino Grand Prix at Misano, Dorna CEO Carmelo Ezpeleta and Paolo Simoncelli announced that MotoGP was retiring the No. 58. “This number, from now, belongs to the Simoncelli family,” Ezpeleta said. That last item matters beyond Simoncelli. The 58 joined Kato’s 74 and Tomizawa’s 48 on the sport’s list of retired numbers, alongside honorary retirements for Kevin Schwantz (34) and Loris Capirossi (65). It is a short list, and three of its five numbers belong to riders killed racing. Only the Simoncelli family can reverse the 58’s retirement, and they have not. Simoncelli’s career numbers (14 Grand Prix wins, 31 podiums and one world title, by one count across all classes) are the stat line. The thing people remember is what the sport lost on a Sunday when he was 24 and in the best form of his career. For where the premier class stands now, see our breakdown of the complete 2027 MotoGP grid . Related Reading on Backfire Racing Today in Motorsport History, October 20: Márquez Is Black-Flagged at Phillip Island as a Tyre Crisis Forces a Bike-Swap Race Racing’s Hidden Costs: The Helmet That Expires Differently in Every Rulebook MotoGP’s 2027 Grid Is Full, and Every Signature Was a Bet on a Bike Nobody Has Raced Today in Motorsport History, October 22: Senna Won on the Road at Suzuka in 1989, but Prost Won the Title Sources: Sepang International Circuit official statement, October 25, 2011; Al Jazeera report, October 23, 2011; Wikipedia entries for the 2011 Malaysian motorcycle Grand Prix and Marco Simoncelli; Dorna/MotoGP announcement of the No. 58 retirement, September 8, 2016. item.description: BLOOMINGTON, IN - OCTOBER 17: Ohio State Buckeyes DE Kenyatta Jackson Jr. (2) and Ohio State Buckeyes WR Jeremiah Smith (4) prior to a college football game between the Ohio State Buckeyes and Indiana Hoosiers on October 17, 2026 at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, IN. (Photo by James Black/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images College football has evolved so rapidly over the last several years, and there are an increasing variety of ways to break down any given Saturday. Here on Scarlet Spreadsheet , we are going to compile all of the various analytical models to get the best possible preview of each of Ohio State’s matchups throughout the 2026 season based on the underlying numbers and metrics. With no opponent for the Buckeyes to match up against this weekend, we will instead take a look at where Ohio State stands against the rest of the college football landscape in terms of both the computer rankings and the advanced statistics. Ryan Day’s group ranks among the top 15 in the country in both total offense and defense, but what do the math and the analytics say about this year’s Ohio State team through their first seven games? item.title: Bears Urged to Cut Ties With $76M Corner, Save $16M for Trade
item.description: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - SEPTEMBER 13: Jaylon Johnson #1 of the Chicago Bears looks on prior to the game against the Carolina Panthers at Bank of America Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) Getty CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 22: Kyler Gordon #6 of the Chicago Bears celebrates with Jaylon Johnson #1 after a third down defensive stop against the New England Patriots during the first quarter of the game at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Getty INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 28: Deforest Buckner #99 of the Indianapolis Colts on field during the second quarter against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on September 28, 2025 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images) Getty The Chicago Bears were able to come away with a 30-24 win over the New England Patriots, but there was one huge concern throughout the game — the play of cornerback Jaylon Johnson. Johnson, who was once regarded as the league’s top cornerback and was given a massive four-year, $76 million extension just two years ago, has looked like a shell of himself to start the 2026 season, and he should have been benched against the Patriots. He’s allowed one of the most yards per reception allowed (17.5) this season among qualified cornerbacks and gave up a few chunk plays against New England. Bears fans were not happy, and didn’t hold back on social media. “I’m over Jaylon Johnson. There is a difference between losing a step and not trying – and he is both right now. I can accept a player just not being good anymore but giving such poor effort is unacceptable. He needs to be benched.” @MattEurich “Cut Jaylon Johnson. We don’t need picks for him. He is ruining this team every week.” @CalebGoatQB1 “It’s time …. You have to bench Jaylon Johnson. Idk what’s the better Answer….. but that’s unacceptable” @PatTheDesigner “If you can go to the Bench for fumbling should be the same for tackling.” @olin_kreutz (Former Bears All-Pro center) Is there a scenario that makes sense for the Bears to cut Johnson? Bears Urged to Cut Ties With Jaylon Johnson Getty CHICAGO, ILLINOIS – OCTOBER 22: Kyler Gordon #6 of the Chicago Bears celebrates with Jaylon Johnson #1 after a third down defensive stop against the New England Patriots during the first quarter of the game at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) According to OvertheCap.com, the Bears can cut Jaylon Johnson and save $16 million in cap space. It would be a tough decision to make, considering the Bears are relatively thin at cornerback, and rookie Malik Muhammad suffered a toe injury against the Patriots, but perhaps the first route Chicago could take is seeing if there are any teams out there who would be potentially interested in trading for him. The likely answer to that scenario is no, so the next course of action could be just benching him

Johnson, who was once regarded as the league’s top cornerback and was given a massive four-year, $76 million extension just two years ago, has looked like a shell of himself to start the 2026 season, and he should have been benched against the Patriots. He’s allowed one of the most yards per reception allowed (17.5) this season among qualified cornerbacks and gave up a few chunk plays against New England. Bears fans were not happy, and didn’t hold back on social media. “I’m over Jaylon Johnson. There is a difference between losing a step and not trying – and he is both right now. I can accept a player just not being good anymore but giving such poor effort is unacceptable. He needs to be benched.” @MattEurich “Cut Jaylon Johnson. We don’t need picks for him. He is ruining this team every week.” @CalebGoatQB1 “It’s time …. You have to bench Jaylon Johnson. Idk what’s the better Answer….. but that’s unacceptable” @PatTheDesigner “If you can go to the Bench for fumbling should be the same for tackling.” @olin_kreutz (Former Bears All-Pro center) Is there a scenario that makes sense for the Bears to cut Johnson? Bears Urged to Cut Ties With Jaylon Johnson Getty CHICAGO, ILLINOIS – OCTOBER 22: Kyler Gordon #6 of the Chicago Bears celebrates with Jaylon Johnson #1 after a third down defensive stop against the New England Patriots during the first quarter of the game at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) According to OvertheCap.com, the Bears can cut Jaylon Johnson and save $16 million in cap space. It would be a tough decision to make, considering the Bears are relatively thin at cornerback, and rookie Malik Muhammad suffered a toe injury against the Patriots, but perhaps the first route Chicago could take is seeing if there are any teams out there who would be potentially interested in trading for him. The likely answer to that scenario is no, so the next course of action could be just benching him outright. However, if the Bears are serious about making a big-time trade before the deadline on November 10th, perhaps the best course of action is cutting Johnson and saving that $16 million in cap space. It would give Chicago a lot more leeway, considering the Bears have just $9.5 million in available cap space as of October 23rd. Potential Trade Targets for the Bears Getty INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA – SEPTEMBER 28: DeForest Buckner #99 of the Indianapolis Colts on field during the second quarter against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on September 28, 2025 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images) Perfect timing because Daniel Popper of The Athletic recently published an article on 50 players who could be dealt before the trade deadline, with the Bears listed as a trade fit for 19 of the following 50: Jeffery Simmons , Defensive Tackle, Titans DeForest Buckner, Defensive Tackle, Colts Tuli Tuipulotu , Edge Rusher, Chargers Vita Vea , Defensive Tackle, Buccaneers Alex Highsmith , Edge Rusher, Steelers Moro Ojomo , Defensive Tackle, Eagles Derwin James , Safety, Chargers Amani Hooker , Safety, Titans Khalil Mack , Edge Rusher, Chargers Daron Payne , Defensive Tackle, Commanders Josh Sweat , Edge Rusher, Cardinals Budda Baker , Safety, Cardinals Grover Stewart , Defensive Tackle, Colts Nolan Smith , Edge Rusher, Eagles Zach Sieler , Defensive Tackle, Dolphins Andre Cisco , Safety, Jets A’Shawn Robinson , Defensive Tackle, Buccaneers Dorance Armstrong Jr., Edge Rusher, Commanders Dalvin Tomlinson , Defensive Tackle, Chargers A dream trade would be Simmons, though the Titans would be reluctant to trade him away considering he’s one of, if not the best, interior defensive linemen in the NFL. Some more realistic options that would fit the Bears’ need and fit on defense are Buckner, Ojomo, Mack, Sweat, and Sieler. There could be other potential trade targets who pique the Bears’ interest as the deadline approaches, but either way, general manager Ryan Poles could make a shocking decision and cut Jaylon Johnson, who signed a major extension just two offseasons ago. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Bears Urged to Cut Ties With $76M Corner, Save $16M for Trade appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Losing to the Bears wasn’t a surprise, it was more about how the Patriots lost | Karen Guregian
item.description: Short week. On the road. A long list of injuries. Good opponent. If there was a recipe for the Patriots win streak to come to an end, this was it. And right on cue, that’s exactly what played out at Soldier Field Thursday night. After ripping off three straight wins, the Patriots hit their breaking point against the Chicago Bears. They were in it to the end. But they did more to lose this game, than win it. As stated above, it was bound to happen given all of the variables. Still, a few alarm bells went off given what transpired during the 30-24 loss. The first alarm? The Patriots gave a clinic on how to miss tackles. It wasn’t just one guy. It was at every level of the defense. In all, they tallied 16 whiffs according to Pro Football Focus. Cornerbacks Marcus Jones (5) and Charles Woods (3) were the worst offenders. But they weren’t alone. Christian Ellis, Robert Spillane, Craig Woodson, Elijah Ponder, Cory Durden and Kevin Byard joined the parade. “Tackling wasn’t good enough, not against this team,” Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said following the loss. “It just leads to extra yards and conversions. We fought, but I would say we need to turn the ball over and we have to tackle better. Those are fundamental skills.” The defense did not turn the ball over. And, they doubled their worst missed tackle total from previous games. Can it all be chalked up to a short week? Alarm bell No. 2? Explosive plays allowed. The defense surrendered seven pass plays of 20 yards or more. Caleb Williams (22 of 33 for 308 yards, 2 TDs) and his wizardry can account for a lot of that. So can the sea of missed tackles. But how many times were the Patriots going to leave Luther Burden III (4 catches, 130 yards) and Colston Loveland (7 catches, 69 yards, 1 TD) wide open? Answer: Too many. Alarm bell No. 3? The Patriots were flagged for 10 penalties. That didn’t help matters, especially trying to come from behind. Four of those came against the offensive line. Both Walter Rouse and Morgan Moses had holding penalties. Will Campbell and Matt Pryor were penalized for false starts. Those were drive killers, especially in the second half. On the other side of the ball, outside linebacker Gabe Jacas made a costly mistake with a late hit on Williams, drawing a roughing the passer penalty, which was added to a 22-yard catch from Burden. Jacas crashed into Williams well after he delivered the football. That’s not what the Patriots are looking for from the rookie. Alarm bell No. 4? A Drake Maye end zone turnover. The Patriots quarterback played brilliantly for the most part, but that one blemish, one that turned up too often in the first three games, came back to haunt the team. Instead of hitting Eli Raridon, Maye underthrew the rookie tight end with a second quarter pass. The ball was intercepted by Bears linebacker D’Marco Jackson. item.content:encoded: Short week. On the road. A long list of injuries. Good opponent. If there was a recipe for the Patriots win streak to come to an end, this was it. And right on cue, that’s exactly what played out at Soldier Field Thursday night. After ripping off three straight wins, the Patriots hit their breaking point against the Chicago Bears. They were in it to the end. But they did more to lose this game, than win it. As stated above, it was bound to happen given all of the variables. Still, a few alarm bells went off given what transpired during the 30-24 loss. The first alarm? The Patriots gave a clinic on how to miss tackles. It wasn’t just one guy. It was at every level of the defense. In all, they tallied 16 whiffs according to Pro Football Focus. Cornerbacks Marcus Jones (5) and Charles Woods (3) were the worst offenders. But they weren’t alone. Christian Ellis, Robert Spillane, Craig Woodson, Elijah Ponder, Cory Durden and Kevin Byard joined the parade. “Tackling wasn’t good enough, not against this team,” Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said following the loss. “It just leads to extra yards and conversions. We fought, but I would say we need to turn the ball over and we have to tackle better. Those are fundamental skills.” The defense did not turn the ball over. And, they doubled their worst missed tackle total from previous games. Can it all be chalked up to a short week? Alarm bell No. 2? Explosive plays allowed. The defense surrendered seven pass plays of 20 yards or more. Caleb Williams (22 of 33 for 308 yards, 2 TDs) and his wizardry can account for a lot of that. So can the sea of missed tackles. But how many times were the Patriots going to leave Luther Burden III (4 catches, 130 yards) and Colston Loveland (7 catches, 69 yards, 1 TD) wide open? Answer: Too many. Alarm bell No. 3? The Patriots were flagged for 10 penalties. That didn’t help matters, especially trying to come from behind. Four of those came against the offensive line. Both Walter Rouse and Morgan Moses had holding penalties. Will Campbell and Matt Pryor were penalized for false starts. Those were drive killers, especially in the second half. On the other side of the ball, outside linebacker Gabe Jacas made a costly mistake with a late hit on Williams, drawing a roughing the passer penalty, which was added to a 22-yard catch from Burden. Jacas crashed into Williams well after he delivered the football. That’s not what the Patriots are looking for from the rookie. Alarm bell No. 4? A Drake Maye end zone turnover. The Patriots quarterback played brilliantly for the most part, but that one blemish, one that turned up too often in the first three games, came back to haunt the team. Instead of hitting Eli Raridon, Maye underthrew the rookie tight end with a second quarter pass. The ball was intercepted by Bears linebacker D’Marco Jackson. The Patriots were in the red zone, the Bears were up 13-7 at the time, and that took points off the board. “It definitely was a huge point of the game,” Maye said. “I just — gosh, it’s those plays I talk about all the time. Those plays that can swing the game, can impact the game, and that was definitely one of them right there. I wish I definitely had that one back.” Maye (24 for 31, 321 yards, 2 TDs, 1 INT) was actually one of the bright spots. He can’t, however, continue to make that kind of mistake. It’s one thing if this was a singular occurrence. The problem is Maye is a repeat offender. Alarm bell No. 5? A.J. Brown was better, but hardly good enough. Coming off one of the worst games of his career (three drops against the Jets), he caught three passes for 48 yards. He was targeted six games. While the attention he drew from the Bears helped others get open, the Patriots need more from their top receiver, and player they surrendered a first-round pick for back in June. Brown was playing in his second game after returning from his stint on the IR with the high ankle sprain he suffered Week 1 in Seattle. While Brown told reporters after the game his ankle felt fine, he doesn’t quite have the explosiveness he showed during training camp. Or when he was with Philadelphia. He’s getting open, but doesn’t seem quite like himself just yet. IF the Patriots are going anywhere, they need the dynamic playmaking version of Brown. And they need it sooner, rather than later. item.title: IndyCar to return to Europe with Barcelona race in 2027
item.description: Motorsport photo IndyCar announced Friday that the IndyCar Series will head to Spain in 2027 for a race at Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya – as Motorsport.com previously confirmed . The inaugural IndyCar Grand Prix of Barcelona is scheduled for Sunday, July 18, 2027. Serving as the centerpiece of Phase Two of the 2027 IndyCar Series schedule, the event will give Barcelona native and five-time champion Alex Palou a home race. The multiyear agreement will be IndyCar’s first race outside North America since 2013, when James Hinchcliffe won on the street circuit of São Paulo, Brazil. It also signals the series' long-awaited return to European soil for the first time since competing at the TT Circuit Assen in the Netherlands in 2007. “This is a monumental day for our sport,” Penske Entertainment Corp. President and CEO Mark Miles said. “We are pleased to be able to take our ultra-competitive brand of wheel-to-wheel racing to Europe and thrilled that we can showcase IndyCar in Alex Palou’s hometown. We have seen Alex’s remarkable skill and talent for several years and know his fans in Spain have been clamoring to watch him race in person. “We cannot wait to see the NTT IndyCar Series compete at one of the world’s most recognizable motorsports venues set against the backdrop of a very historic and breathtaking international destination like Barcelona.” Palou, 29, won his fifth IndyCar Series championship in 2026. The Chip Ganassi Racing driver became only the second racer in series history to secure four consecutive titles, joining Sebastien Bourdais (2004–07). Boasting five championships in six years and 25 career victories – putting him tied for 17th on the all-time wins list – Palou trails only A.J. Foyt (seven) and teammate Scott Dixon (six) for most titles in series history. “I’m so excited to be part of IndyCar’s first race in Barcelona,” Palou said. “It is an amazing opportunity, and it means so much to me to have a race at home in Barcelona, it’s hard to put into words. I know the fans are going to love it, and I think we are going to put on a great show. We’re going to try hard with the team at Chip Ganassi Racing to bring home the trophy in July.” Located in Montmeló just outside Barcelona, Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya has been a premier international racing venue since opening in 1991. The venue has historically hosted elite championships, including FIA Formula One and MotoGP, and is celebrated globally for its high-speed corners and technical, demanding layout. For local organizers, adding IndyCar fits into a broader strategy to diversify and elevate the venue's world-class offerings. "The arrival of IndyCar is a major milestone and an exciting challenge for the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya," said Pau Relat, Chairman of the Board of Fira de Barcelona and Fira Circuit. For local organizers, adding IndyCar fits into a broader strategy to diversify and elevate the venue's world-class offerings. "The arrival of IndyCar is a major milestone and an exciting challenge for the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya," said Pau Relat, Chairman of the Board of Fira de Barcelona and Fira Circuit. "Bringing one of the most prestigious and spectacular championships in global motorsport to our venue strengthens our international positioning, connects us with new audiences and markets, and reinforces our strategy of diversifying the circuit’s activity through world-class events. IndyCar officials noted that the complete Phase Two lineup of the 2027 schedule – including the full listing of races and official broadcast tune-in times – will be announced later. item.title: WNBA’s Houston Comets find local broadcasting homes for returning season
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Houston Comets return to the WNBA next season, and they’ve already found a local broadcasting home. On Thursday, the Comets and Tegna announced a multi-year deal that will make it easy for anyone in the Houston market to find games. KTBU Channel 55 and CBS affiliate KHOU 11 (select games) will broadcast Comet games on free TV, while Space City Home Network will simulcast on cable, DirecTV, DirecTV Stream, and Fubo. The network’s direct-to-consumer product, SCHN+, will also stream all games. “Bringing the Comets back to Houston is about reigniting the passion, pride, and energy that have always connected this organization with its fans and community,” said Gretchen Sheirr, President of Business Operations for the Houston Rockets and Comets. “As the WNBA continues to reach new heights, we’re thrilled to partner with TEGNA to make Comets basketball more accessible to fans across the Houston area through free, over-the-air broadcasts on KTBU and additional coverage on KHOU. We’re excited to bring fans closer to the action and deliver outstanding coverage as we begin this exciting new chapter in Comets history.” According to a press release, KHOU will also create exclusive Comets content year-round, providing coverage across its newscasts, 24/7 streaming channel, and digital platforms. “KHOU has covered Houston sports for decades, and the Comets’ homecoming is a story we’ve been waiting to tell,” said David Loving, KHOU’s president and general manager. “As a founding partner, we’re ready to bring Comets action to fans across the region.” The Houston Comets were one of the WNBA’s original eight franchises and won the league’s first four championships. Despite that, the league folded the franchise in 2008 during the height of the Great Recession. This year, the Fertitta family, owners of the NBA’s Houston Rockets, purchased the Connecticut Sun and relocated the team to Houston as the new Houston Comets. Longtime ESPN NBA reporter Kevin Pelton joined the Houston Comets’ front office earlier this year. The post WNBA’s Houston Comets find local broadcasting homes for returning season appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: 5 NFL Trades to Help Rebuild The Indianapolis Colts
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Indianapolis Colts parted ways with general manager Chris Ballard at the start of the week, a move that should prove to be the first step toward an overhaul of the franchise. While additional firings will likely come in January, the 2026 NFL trade deadline provides Indianapolis with another opportunity to reset things and focus on the future. Amid swirling rumors about potential players Indianapolis could trade in the next few weeks, we’re proposing a few NFL trades that could help start a rebuild for the Colts. Josh Downs Traded to Seattle Seahawks Sep 27, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs (2) runs with the ball after a catch against the Houston Texans in the first half at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images A Keenan Allen trade would also make sense for Indianapolis, but it stands to reason there would be more league-wide interest in Josh Downs. Like Allen, he’s a half-season rental, but the acquiring team would also get the chance to see if the 25-year-old wide receiver can be a long-term fit in their offense. Standing at 5-foot-9, Downs has played 172 snaps (53.4 percent) out of the slot this season with Indianapolis. Downs would be an intriguing fit for the Seattle Seahawks. Indianapolis Colts trade: Josh Downs Seattle Seahawks trade: 2027 5th Round Pick Seattle’s receiving corps needs some help. Rashid Shaheed has produced just 350 receiving yards in 15 games since the team acquired him a year ago and 33-year-old wideout Cooper Kupp has been a non-factor at times. Downs is capable of getting open quickly and could provide Sam Darnold with an alternative to Jaxon Smith-Njigba at a time when Seattle’s passing game doesn’t seem to have a ton of viable alternatives. Las Vegas Raiders Acquire DeForest Buckner Oct 4, 2026; Tottenham, United Kingdom; Indianapolis Colts defensive tackle DeForest Buckner (99) and defensive tackle Grover Stewart (90) react as Washington Commanders quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis (16) watches in the second half during the 2026 NFL London Games at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Six years ago, Indianapolis acquired DeForest Buckner from the San Francisco 49ers in exchange for a first-round pick. The veteran defensive tackle remains a very effective disruptor on the interior and given that he’s in a contract year, the 32-year-old should have a strong market of suitors. If Indianapolis wants to keep him out of the division (Houston Texans), one fit we do like for the veteran is the Las Vegas Raiders. Josh Downs Traded to Seattle Seahawks Sep 27, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs (2) runs with the ball after a catch against the Houston Texans in the first half at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images A Keenan Allen trade would also make sense for Indianapolis, but it stands to reason there would be more league-wide interest in Josh Downs. Indianapolis Colts trade: Josh Downs Seattle Seahawks trade: 2027 5th Round Pick Seattle’s receiving corps needs some help. Las Vegas Raiders Acquire DeForest Buckner Oct 4, 2026; Tottenham, United Kingdom; Indianapolis Colts defensive tackle DeForest Buckner (99) and defensive tackle Grover Stewart (90) react as Washington Commanders quarterback Athan Kaliakmanis (16) watches in the second half during the 2026 NFL London Games at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Six years ago, Indianapolis acquired DeForest Buckner from the San Francisco 49ers in exchange for a first-round pick. The veteran defensive tackle remains a very effective disruptor on the interior and given that he’s in a contract year, the 32-year-old should have a strong market of suitors. If Indianapolis wants to keep him out of the division (Houston Texans), one fit we do like for the veteran is the Las Vegas Raiders. Las Vegas Raiders trade: 2027 4th Round Pick Indianapolis Colts trade: DeForest Buckner Buckner would provide a significant boost to a Raiders defensive line that currently ranks 26th in ESPN pass-rush win rate (45 percent). He would also greatly benefit from playing alongside Maxx Crosby, giving himself a great chance at finishing this season with seven-plus sacks for the first time since 2023. Buckner’s addition would also increase the Raiders’ chances of potentially sneaking into the postseason as a wild card team. Quenton Nelson Lands with Green Bay Packers Sep 27, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Indianapolis Colts guard Quenton Nelson (56) practices before the game at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images A total teardown is unlikely, so we’d be far more surprised than not if Indianapolis traded the likes of Quenton Nelson and Jonathan Taylor. With that said, now might be the time for the Colts to move their former All-Pro guard to a contender in dire need of help on the interior offensive line since Nelson might not re-sign with Indianapolis next offseason anyway. Indianapolis Colts trade: Quenton Nelson Green Bay Packers trade: 2028 3rd Round Pick While the Green Bay Packers offensive line isn’t as historically bad as it was to start the season, it still has major problems on the interior. Veteran Kevin Zeitler should still eventually start at right guard, but Aaron Banks’ durability issues are still keeping him off the field. Nelson isn’t an All-Pro caliber player at this point, but he would represent a monumental upgrade on the interior for Green Bay. When Jordan Love has been given a semblance of a clean pocket, he’s been lights-out this season. Los Angeles Rams Pick Up Spencer Shrader Oct 18, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Indianapolis Colts kicker Spencer Shrader (3) during the first half against the Tennessee Titans at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images Colts kicker Spencer Shrader leads the NFL in points scored (66), converting on all 18 of his field-goal attempts this season, including 8-for-8 from 40-plus yards away. While kicker trades are a rarity in the NFL during the season, the right level of desperation from a team can change that. Enter the Los Angeles Rams. Indianapolis Colts trade: Spencer Shrader Los Angeles Rams trade: 2027 5th Round Pick The beauty of acquiring Shrader for Los Angeles is that he’s a restricted free agent in 2027, so this can be a multi-season solution to kicking woes that have long haunted this franchise. While trading a fifth-round pick for a kicker might feel steep, it becomes easier to justify when you consider the Rams would probably be 4-2 right now instead of 2-4 if they had a reliable kicker from the start. Jonathan Taylor Dealt to Minnesota Vikings Oct 18, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor (28) runs with the ball against Tennessee Titans safety Amani Hooker (37) during the second half at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images Given ownership’s recent offseason investment in Taylor, it would be a shock if the All-Pro running back is dealt by the NFL trade deadline. However, teams are going to make inquiries, and he might be the perfect offensive weapon to make the Minnesota Vikings the team to beat in the NFC. Indianapolis Colts trade: Jonathan Taylor Minnesota Vikings trade: 2027 2nd Round Pick, Jauan Jennings, 2028 4th Round Pick Taylor’s three-down ability would make him the perfect featured back in Kevin O’Connell’s offense, and he would also thrive sharing the backfield with quarterback Kyler Murray. Minnesota already has the run blocking to maximize Taylor, and with defenses already forced to account for Justin Jefferson, that would also mean lighter boxes for Taylor to run against.
