item.title: Man Utd defeat to Como ‘unacceptable’, says Carrick
item.description: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick admitted on Friday his side have “lost their way” after a 4-1 thrashing by Champions League debutants Como made it seven games without a win. After a successful interim spell in charge in the second half of last season, Carrick was appointed on a permanent basis just five months ago, but his position is at risk ahead of Sunday’s visit of Bournemouth to Old Trafford. United are off to their worst start in the Premier League era, were dumped out of the League Cup by Brighton and have lost two of their opening three Champions League games. “Recently we haven’t had a good time. I totally accept that. We had five months of relative success in a spell where I was happy with a lot of things we were doing as a team,” Carrick said in an impassioned address at the start of his press conference on Friday. “We haven’t done well enough lately. We’ve had a spell we’re really not happy with. Como was a bad night. It hurt me. It was really unacceptable. “The supporters have to make the effort and spend the money to come and watch us. To have the feeling we all had after the game was a tough moment.” Carrick added: “My job is to put a team on the pitch that represents the supporters and that they can be proud of the identity we show. We have gone away from that recently in certain games which I am fully aware of and definintely doing something about.” AFP The post Man Utd defeat to Como ‘unacceptable’, says Carrick appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: I once wanted to be a DJ – UK’s Prince William
item.description: Prince William has made a rare royal appearance on a BBC chat show, with the heir to the throne confessing he would have liked to join the police or be a DJ. The Prince of Wales appeared on an episode set to air Friday evening, to promote his Earthshot Prize, which goes to environmental causes. The show’s host, comedian Graham Norton, is known for his A-list guests and mildly ribbing celebrities. Wearing a blue suit, shirt and tie, William was roaring with laughter in images released ahead of the show on his and his wife’s Instagram. He sat on the show’s sofa next to actresses Cate Blanchett and Hannah Waddingham and conservationist Robert Irwin, all involved in the prize. Hello! magazine wrote that William is the first working royal to appear on a British talk show although Sarah Ferguson, the former wife of William’s uncle, the former prince Andrew, was interviewed by Norton when she still had a royal title. The Graham Norton Show is now in its 33rd series and is the broadcaster’s most watched chat show. Recent guests include Madonna. The BBC reported there were “cheers and gasps from the audience” when William appeared as a surprise guest. He will present the Earthshot Prize in Mumbai on November 17. Launched in 2020, the prize supports initiatives that help tackle environmental crises such as climate change. As with previous competitions, this year’s winners will receive one million pounds ($1.3 million) each “to accelerate the impact of their innovative solutions”, organisers said. William was asked whether he ever fantasised about another job rather than becoming king, telling Norton: “I did want to be a policeman when I was younger. I thought I could make a good one,” adding that he also went through “a phase of wanting to be a DJ — I wasn’t very good.” William spoke of his family’s love for “The Celebrity Traitors”, a devious reality show currently topping ratings. He also said he was a “big fan” of director Christopher Nolan’s “Dark Knight” trilogy about Batman, which he called “psychologically dark and deep”. The prince has kept tight-lipped about the return to Britain of his estranged brother Prince Harry, who said in an interview this week with GQ magazine that he wanted things to “work out” with his father, King Charles III, and William, his elder brother. AFP The post I once wanted to be a DJ – UK’s Prince William appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Malaria: Nigeria’s prevalence drops to 15.2%, FG targets 50% reduction by 2030
item.description: By Chioma Obinna The Federal Government has reported a decline in malaria parasite prevalence among children aged six to 59 months from 22 per cent in 2021 to 15.2 per cent in 2025, while setting a target to halve malaria prevalence and malaria-attributable deaths by 2030. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, disclosed this on Thursday at the launch of the 2025 Nigeria Malaria Indicator Survey (NMIS) Report and the National Malaria Strategic Plan 2026–2030 in Abuja. Pate, who was represented by the ministry’s Permanent Secretary, Daju Kachollom, said the 6.8 percentage-point decline reflected progress in the country’s malaria control efforts but warned that the gains must be sustained. He said the Federal Government was targeting a 50 per cent reduction in malaria prevalence and malaria-attributable deaths from their respective 2025 levels by 2030. The minister, however, cautioned against interpreting the decline as evidence that malaria had been brought under control nationwide, stressing the need for stronger prevention, surveillance and funding. He cited Kebbi State as an example of significant improvement, with malaria prevalence reportedly dropping from 49 per cent in 2021 to 18 per cent in 2025. Pate said the findings underscored the importance of using reliable data to identify high-burden communities and direct interventions where they would have the greatest impact. Bed-net use remains a concern The minister also highlighted the need to improve the consistent use of insecticide-treated nets, a major tool for preventing malaria transmission. According to the survey findings, 72.3 per cent of children and 80.6 per cent of pregnant women in households that owned insecticide-treated nets slept under one. He said the figures demonstrated the need to strengthen public awareness and ensure that households translated access to preventive tools into consistent use. New strategy targets high-burden areas Pate said the National Malaria Strategic Plan 2026–2030 was aligned with the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative and would be implemented through the Sector-Wide Approach, guided by the principle of “One Plan, One Budget, One Report, One Conversation.” He explained that the plan’s sub-national tailoring approach would enable authorities to direct resources and interventions according to the malaria burden and epidemiological circumstances of individual states and communities. The minister urged state governments to take ownership of their respective survey findings, align malaria control plans and budgets with identified needs, and ensure timely release of funds. He also called on development partners to align their financial and technical support with national priorities. item.dc:creator: Urowayino Jeremiah
item.content:encoded: By Chioma Obinna The Federal Government has reported a decline in malaria parasite prevalence among children aged six to 59 months from 22 per cent in 2021 to 15.2 per cent in 2025, while setting a target to halve malaria prevalence and malaria-attributable deaths by 2030. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, disclosed this on Thursday at the launch of the 2025 Nigeria Malaria Indicator Survey (NMIS) Report and the National Malaria Strategic Plan 2026–2030 in Abuja. Pate, who was represented by the ministry’s Permanent Secretary, Daju Kachollom, said the 6.8 percentage-point decline reflected progress in the country’s malaria control efforts but warned that the gains must be sustained. He said the Federal Government was targeting a 50 per cent reduction in malaria prevalence and malaria-attributable deaths from their respective 2025 levels by 2030. The minister, however, cautioned against interpreting the decline as evidence that malaria had been brought under control nationwide, stressing the need for stronger prevention, surveillance and funding. He cited Kebbi State as an example of significant improvement, with malaria prevalence reportedly dropping from 49 per cent in 2021 to 18 per cent in 2025. Pate said the findings underscored the importance of using reliable data to identify high-burden communities and direct interventions where they would have the greatest impact. Bed-net use remains a concern The minister also highlighted the need to improve the consistent use of insecticide-treated nets, a major tool for preventing malaria transmission. According to the survey findings, 72.3 per cent of children and 80.6 per cent of pregnant women in households that owned insecticide-treated nets slept under one. He said the figures demonstrated the need to strengthen public awareness and ensure that households translated access to preventive tools into consistent use. New strategy targets high-burden areas Pate said the National Malaria Strategic Plan 2026–2030 was aligned with the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative and would be implemented through the Sector-Wide Approach, guided by the principle of “One Plan, One Budget, One Report, One Conversation.” He explained that the plan’s sub-national tailoring approach would enable authorities to direct resources and interventions according to the malaria burden and epidemiological circumstances of individual states and communities. The minister urged state governments to take ownership of their respective survey findings, align malaria control plans and budgets with identified needs, and ensure timely release of funds. He also called on development partners to align their financial and technical support with national priorities. NPC calls for data-driven interventions The Director-General of the National Population Commission, Dr Abuh Muhammed, said the survey demonstrated the value of collaboration between the National Malaria Elimination Programme and the commission. He said the partnership combined technical expertise in malaria control with the commission’s survey infrastructure and field operations, providing evidence to guide national planning. Muhammed reaffirmed the commission’s commitment to supporting evidence-based policymaking and urged government officials and development partners to use the findings to direct resources to areas with the greatest need. Pate commended the National Malaria Elimination Programme, the National Population Commission and other partners involved in producing the survey. He reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to strengthening domestic financing, improving surveillance and sustaining coordinated action to reduce malaria cases and deaths. The 2030 target will require sustained investment in prevention, early diagnosis, effective treatment and routine health services, alongside targeted interventions in communities where malaria transmission remains high. item.title: Ogogo’s daughters announce Nollywood plans, pledge to sustain father’s legacy
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The daughters of late Nollywood actor Taiwo Hassan, popularly known as Ogogo, say they plan to pursue careers in the film industry and continue their father’s legacy. Taiwo Halima Olamide, known as Lima Ogogo, and her sister, Shakirat Taiwo, popularly called Kira Ogogo, announced their plans in an appreciation video shared on social media on Wednesday, October 21. The sisters also thanked Nigerians and members of the entertainment industry for supporting their family following their father’s death. “You guys loved our daddy so much. This is an appreciation video to tell you people thank you,” they said. Lima, speaking on behalf of the family, added: “On behalf of my family and I, we want to say thank you very much to everybody who stood by us.” The sisters acknowledged support from several public figures, including Honourable Tayo Ayinde, the First Lady, the Ogun State governor, Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, and the Olu of Ilaro. They also thanked those who sent messages of condolence during the family’s period of mourning. They said their entry into Nollywood would be a lasting commitment, rather than a one-off tribute to their father. “We are going to start seeing Ogogo through my sister Kira Ogogo. We are coming to the industry, and we’re here to stay,” Lima said. The sisters urged fans who enjoyed Ogogo’s films to support their upcoming projects by watching and sharing their content, particularly on Kira Ogogo’s YouTube channel, KiraOgogoTV. Ogogo, a prominent figure in Yoruba cinema, died on August 23, 2026, aged 66. He was buried the following day in Ilaro, Ogun State, according to Islamic rites. His death drew tributes from Nollywood colleagues and admirers. The post Ogogo’s daughters announce Nollywood plans, pledge to sustain father’s legacy appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 14 countries offering visa on arrival to Nigerians in 2026
item.description: Nigerian passport holders can travel to several countries where they can obtain a visa upon arrival, eliminating the need to secure a conventional visa from an embassy before departure. The destinations span Africa, Asia, the Middle East and the Pacific, offering options for Nigerians planning holidays, business trips and other short visits. A visa on arrival (VoA) allows eligible travellers to obtain a visa at an authorised airport, seaport or border crossing. However, the facility does not automatically guarantee entry, as immigration officials may require supporting documents and evidence that visitors meet the country’s entry conditions. According to VisaChecker’s September 2026 data, 14 destinations offer visa-on-arrival access to Nigerian passport holders. Passport Index also identifies several destinations under this category, although the figures reported by different databases vary. Here are 14 countries Nigerians can consider when planning international trips. African countries offering visa on arrival to Nigerians 1. Burundi Burundi, an East African country known for its mountainous landscapes and Lake Tanganyika, offers Nigerian passport holders a visa-on-arrival option. Passport Index lists the facility as allowing stays of up to 30 days. Travellers should confirm whether advance authorisation or additional documentation is required before departure. 2. Comoros Comoros, an island nation in the Indian Ocean off the eastern coast of Africa, is another destination Nigerians can access through a visa-on-arrival arrangement. Passport Index lists a permitted stay of up to 45 days for eligible Nigerian visitors. Travellers should verify the applicable fees and entry procedures before travelling. 3. Djibouti Djibouti, located in the Horn of Africa, offers Nigerian passport holders visa-on-arrival and electronic visa options, according to Passport Index. The database lists a maximum stay of up to 90 days under the visa-on-arrival category. Travellers should confirm which application route applies to their circumstances and intended port of entry. 4. Madagascar Madagascar, an island country off the southeastern coast of Africa, is known for its distinctive wildlife, rainforests and beaches. Nigerian passport holders are listed as eligible for visa-on-arrival access, with Passport Index indicating a stay of up to 90 days. An electronic visa is also listed as an option. Travellers should check the latest requirements before choosing between the available routes. 5. Mauritius Mauritius is a popular Indian Ocean destination known for its beaches, lagoons and resorts. The destinations span Africa, Asia, the Middle East and the Pacific, offering options for Nigerians planning holidays, business trips and other short visits. A visa on arrival (VoA) allows eligible travellers to obtain a visa at an authorised airport, seaport or border crossing. However, the facility does not automatically guarantee entry, as immigration officials may require supporting documents and evidence that visitors meet the country’s entry conditions. According to VisaChecker’s September 2026 data, 14 destinations offer visa-on-arrival access to Nigerian passport holders. Passport Index also identifies several destinations under this category, although the figures reported by different databases vary. Here are 14 countries Nigerians can consider when planning international trips. African countries offering visa on arrival to Nigerians 1. Burundi Burundi, an East African country known for its mountainous landscapes and Lake Tanganyika, offers Nigerian passport holders a visa-on-arrival option. Passport Index lists the facility as allowing stays of up to 30 days. Travellers should confirm whether advance authorisation or additional documentation is required before departure. 2. Comoros Comoros, an island nation in the Indian Ocean off the eastern coast of Africa, is another destination Nigerians can access through a visa-on-arrival arrangement. Passport Index lists a permitted stay of up to 45 days for eligible Nigerian visitors. Travellers should verify the applicable fees and entry procedures before travelling. 3. Djibouti Djibouti, located in the Horn of Africa, offers Nigerian passport holders visa-on-arrival and electronic visa options, according to Passport Index. The database lists a maximum stay of up to 90 days under the visa-on-arrival category. Travellers should confirm which application route applies to their circumstances and intended port of entry. 4. Madagascar Madagascar, an island country off the southeastern coast of Africa, is known for its distinctive wildlife, rainforests and beaches. Nigerian passport holders are listed as eligible for visa-on-arrival access, with Passport Index indicating a stay of up to 90 days. An electronic visa is also listed as an option. Travellers should check the latest requirements before choosing between the available routes. 5. Mauritius Mauritius is a popular Indian Ocean destination known for its beaches, lagoons and resorts. Passport Index lists visa-on-arrival access for Nigerian citizens for stays of up to 14 days. Because the permitted period is relatively short, travellers intending to stay longer should establish the appropriate immigration route before booking. 6. Mozambique Mozambique, located in southeastern Africa, offers Nigerian passport holders a visa-on-arrival option. Passport Index lists a maximum stay of up to 30 days. Visitors should confirm the conditions attached to the facility and ensure they have the necessary travel documents before departure. Asian and Middle Eastern countries offering visa on arrival 7. Cambodia Cambodia, in Southeast Asia, is known for its historical temples, including the Angkor Wat complex, as well as its cultural attractions. Passport Index lists both an electronic visa and visa-on-arrival options for Nigerian passport holders, with the latter allowing stays of up to 30 days. Travellers should confirm the approved entry points, applicable fees and documentation requirements before travelling. 8. Iran Iran is listed among destinations offering Nigerian passport holders a visa-on-arrival option. However, travellers should exercise particular care when checking current entry rules, eligible entry points and any prior approval requirements. They should also review relevant travel advisories before making arrangements. 9. Lebanon Lebanon, on the eastern coast of the Mediterranean Sea, is another destination listed as offering visa-on-arrival access to Nigerian passport holders. Passport Index lists a stay of up to 30 days. Additional requirements may apply, and travellers should confirm their eligibility directly with Lebanese authorities or the relevant diplomatic mission before departure. 10. Maldives The Maldives offers a 30-day tourist visa on arrival to visitors of all nationalities, subject to immigration requirements. According to the Maldives Immigration Service, tourists do not need pre-approval for this visa. However, visitors must have a machine-readable passport with at least one month of validity, confirmed return or onward tickets, a prepaid booking at a registered tourist facility and sufficient funds, or an approved sponsorship arrangement. Travellers must also complete the required Traveller Declaration electronically within 96 hours before arrival. Meeting the requirements does not guarantee admission, which remains subject to immigration clearance. 11. Timor-Leste Timor-Leste, a Southeast Asian country occupying the eastern part of Timor island, offers visa-on-arrival access to eligible visitors. The country’s tourism information states that tourists arriving at Presidente Nicolau Lobato International Airport in Dili can generally obtain a 30-day visa on arrival for US$30. Travellers should have a passport valid for at least six months, a return or onward ticket, proof of accommodation and sufficient funds. An online arrival declaration is also required. Different procedures may apply to those entering through land borders. Pacific and island destinations offering visa on arrival 12. Palau Palau, an island country in the western Pacific Ocean, offers a 30-day tourist visa on arrival, according to published entry guidance. Visitors may be required to show proof of onward or return travel. They must also complete the country’s entry form within 72 hours before arrival and sign the Palau Pledge, a commitment to protect the country’s natural environment and respect local traditions. Nigerians should confirm the latest requirements with Palau’s Bureau of Immigration before travelling. 13. Samoa Samoa, an island country in the South Pacific, allows visitors to apply for a visitor permit on arrival. Its Ministry of the Prime Minister and Cabinet states that visitors can apply for a permit valid for up to 90 days using the arrival card. Travellers must have a passport valid for at least six months beyond their intended stay, a confirmed return or onward ticket, any necessary visa for their next destination, sufficient funds and a confirmed residential contact address. Employment is not permitted under the visitor permit. 14. Tuvalu Tuvalu, a small island nation in the Pacific Ocean, is also listed by Passport Index as offering visa-on-arrival access to Nigerian passport holders, with a stay of up to 30 days. Travellers should confirm the latest entry conditions, available entry points and any documentation requirements with the relevant authorities before booking flights. What Nigerians should know before travelling Although a visa on arrival can make international travel more convenient, it does not mean a traveller can board a flight without preparation. Nigerian passport holders should take the following steps before travelling: 1. Confirm eligibility. Check the destination’s official immigration website or contact its embassy to establish whether Nigerian ordinary passport holders qualify for a visa on arrival. 2. Check passport validity. Many countries require passports to remain valid for at least six months, although the rules differ by destination. 3. Prepare supporting documents. These may include confirmed return tickets, accommodation bookings, evidence of sufficient funds and details of the purpose of the visit. 4. Check entry points. item.title: New tax laws: Commercial drivers still face multiple highway taxes — NURTW
item.description: …Tax Ombud pledges fairness, transparency in tax administration By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief Commercial drivers across Nigeria are still being subjected to multiple highway taxes despite the Federal Government’s tax reforms aimed at eliminating the practice, the National Union of Road Transport Workers (NURTW) has said. The union lamented that a driver travelling from Calabar to Kano could spend as much as ₦300,000 on the road on various taxes and levies imposed by different collectors. The NURTW made the allegation at a stakeholders’ engagement forum on tax administration in Abuja on Friday, calling on the three tiers of government to urgently end the practice, which it said was imposing a heavy burden on transport operators and undermining the economy. Speaking on behalf of the union’s National President, Alh. Musiliu Akinsanya, popularly known as MC Oluomo, Suleiman Danzaki, the Senior Special Adviser on Intergovernmental and International Affairs, said commercial drivers were yet to experience any significant change in the multiple taxation of their operations nationwide. “A driver travelling from Calabar to Kano will spend as much as ₦300,000 on the road before he can get to his destination because of the various people on the road collecting various types of taxes,” Danzaki said. He expressed concern that, apart from overburdening transport operators, the practice could also be depriving governments of revenue, as some collectors allegedly issued receipts printed privately rather than official government receipts. item.dc:creator: Henry Oduah
item.content:encoded: …Tax Ombud pledges fairness, transparency in tax administration By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief Commercial drivers across Nigeria are still being subjected to multiple highway taxes despite the Federal Government’s tax reforms aimed at eliminating the practice, the National Union of Road Transport Workers (NURTW) has said. The union lamented that a driver travelling from Calabar to Kano could spend as much as ₦300,000 on the road on various taxes and levies imposed by different collectors. The NURTW made the allegation at a stakeholders’ engagement forum on tax administration in Abuja on Friday, calling on the three tiers of government to urgently end the practice, which it said was imposing a heavy burden on transport operators and undermining the economy. Speaking on behalf of the union’s National President, Alh. Musiliu Akinsanya, popularly known as MC Oluomo, Suleiman Danzaki, the Senior Special Adviser on Intergovernmental and International Affairs, said commercial drivers were yet to experience any significant change in the multiple taxation of their operations nationwide. “A driver travelling from Calabar to Kano will spend as much as ₦300,000 on the road before he can get to his destination because of the various people on the road collecting various types of taxes,” Danzaki said. He expressed concern that, apart from overburdening transport operators, the practice could also be depriving governments of revenue, as some collectors allegedly issued receipts printed privately rather than official government receipts. Danzaki urged the federal, state and local governments to take immediate and coordinated action to eliminate multiple taxation, warning that the burden on commercial drivers had wider implications for the cost of transportation, the movement of goods and the nation’s economy. However, the Tax Ombud, Dr. John Nwabueze, assured taxpayers that his office was working to promote fairness, transparency and accountability in the country’s tax administration. Nwabueze spoke at the forum, themed “Promoting Fairness in Tax and Revenue Administration in Nigeria,” which was organised to gather complaints and identify challenges confronting taxpayers, with a view to improving compliance and ensuring a more efficient tax system. He said the tax reforms, which commenced in January 2026, were designed to simplify compliance, strengthen revenue mobilisation, support eligible small businesses and promote transparency and accountability. However, he stressed that the success of the reforms would depend not only on the quality of the laws but also on their fair and consistent implementation. “Fairness is not a favour to taxpayers; it is the foundation of public trust and sustainable revenue mobilisation,” he said. According to him, taxpayers are more likely to comply voluntarily when they are treated fairly, understand their obligations and have access to impartial channels for resolving disputes. Conversely, he warned that arbitrary assessments, overlapping levies and inconsistent enforcement could undermine public confidence in the tax system. Nwabueze said the establishment of the Office of the Tax Ombud under the Joint Revenue Board of Nigeria (Establishment) Act, 2025, marked a significant milestone in protecting taxpayers’ rights and strengthening accountability in tax administration. He said the office was mandated to promote lawful, reasonable, transparent and fair administrative processes while encouraging constructive dialogue and accountability among taxpayers and revenue authorities. Since its establishment, he added, the office had made progress in developing a digital complaints management framework, building stakeholder partnerships, introducing taxpayer education initiatives and establishing a dedicated call centre. “Our priority now is to expand access, strengthen operational capacity and ensure that taxpayers know where to turn when they experience administrative difficulties,” he said. The Tax Ombud identified five pillars of fairness required to balance the government’s revenue needs with the rights and dignity of taxpayers. They are equity and proportionality; procedural justice; professionalism, courtesy and respect in tax administration; transparency and accountability; and the protection of vulnerable taxpayers. He urged tax authorities to translate the principles into practical improvements in taxpayers’ everyday experiences by applying the law consistently, communicating obligations clearly and treating taxpayers with dignity. The engagement came amid concerns over the effectiveness of tax reforms in addressing longstanding complaints about multiple levies, overlapping demands and the conduct of revenue collectors across the country. item.title: One-on-One with 2027 APC Presidential Campaign Council member, Segun Sowunmi
item.description: In this interview, Segun Sowunmi assesses the 2027 presidential race, starting with President Bola Tinubu’s chances and moving on to the main challengers. He argues that Atiku Abubakar suffers from an “Emir complex” and lacks the capacity to empathise with poor Nigerians. On Peter Obi, he says the Obidient movement has made enemies of nearly everybody. He describes Seyi Makinde as a politician who burns bridges. He also criticises Atiku’s running mate, Rotimi Amaechi, for politicising his mother’s death. Watch the full conversation for his take on where the race stands. The post One-on-One with 2027 APC Presidential Campaign Council member, Segun Sowunmi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: France to deploy 70,000 police ahead of new protests
item.description: France will deploy some 70,000 police nationwide as it braces for new protests this weekend after some of the worst urban violence in years erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations a week ago, the government said Friday. President Emmanuel Macron, who according to aides is postponing a visit later this month to Nigeria and Senegal amid the crisis, held a meeting of his defence council of top ministers and officials and was to meet security forces. He was also set to host for the first time representatives of high school pupils, whose protests over conditions at their schools sparked the movement that has broadened into a nationwide show of anger against the government at the rising cost of living. Some 70,000 security personnel will be deployed on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said at a press conference in Paris, warning that calls for violence and looting were circulating on social media. The protests have come at a critical moment for France six months ahead of elections to replace Macron, with a new poll underlining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen is the frontrunner and showing her position has been strengthened by the latest events. Adding to tensions, Le Pen is at the weekend due to host her National Rally (RN) party congress in Orleans, with thousands of supporters expected but local authorities fearing clashes as opponents head to the city. Nunez was expected to visit the city Friday to “inspect the security arrangements” at the request of the prime minister’s office, it said. At Macron’s meeting with students, “we will present our demands to him — which remain the same: the state of school infrastructure and an overhaul of the Parcoursup (university admissions) system,” Nathanael Combary, president of Renouveau Lyceen (High School Renewal) told AFP. Macron’s government has sought to draw a line between the legitimate demands of protesters and the looting, burning and ransacking that erupted on the sidelines of protests last Saturday. In a judicial response of unprecedented firmness, courts have already sent 217 people, half of them first-time offenders, to prison over the events on Saturday, Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said. On Thursday, Macron called for “the utmost severity” against “acts of delinquency”, accusing “ultra-left” groups of having sought to “bring down the republic” last weekend. – ‘Police have a responsibility’ – On Saturday, a second round of demonstrations is expected across France. item.content:encoded: France will deploy some 70,000 police nationwide as it braces for new protests this weekend after some of the worst urban violence in years erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations a week ago, the government said Friday. President Emmanuel Macron, who according to aides is postponing a visit later this month to Nigeria and Senegal amid the crisis, held a meeting of his defence council of top ministers and officials and was to meet security forces. He was also set to host for the first time representatives of high school pupils, whose protests over conditions at their schools sparked the movement that has broadened into a nationwide show of anger against the government at the rising cost of living. Some 70,000 security personnel will be deployed on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said at a press conference in Paris, warning that calls for violence and looting were circulating on social media. The protests have come at a critical moment for France six months ahead of elections to replace Macron, with a new poll underlining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen is the frontrunner and showing her position has been strengthened by the latest events. Adding to tensions, Le Pen is at the weekend due to host her National Rally (RN) party congress in Orleans, with thousands of supporters expected but local authorities fearing clashes as opponents head to the city. Nunez was expected to visit the city Friday to “inspect the security arrangements” at the request of the prime minister’s office, it said. At Macron’s meeting with students, “we will present our demands to him — which remain the same: the state of school infrastructure and an overhaul of the Parcoursup (university admissions) system,” Nathanael Combary, president of Renouveau Lyceen (High School Renewal) told AFP. Macron’s government has sought to draw a line between the legitimate demands of protesters and the looting, burning and ransacking that erupted on the sidelines of protests last Saturday. In a judicial response of unprecedented firmness, courts have already sent 217 people, half of them first-time offenders, to prison over the events on Saturday, Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said. On Thursday, Macron called for “the utmost severity” against “acts of delinquency”, accusing “ultra-left” groups of having sought to “bring down the republic” last weekend. – ‘Police have a responsibility’ – On Saturday, a second round of demonstrations is expected across France. Lyon’s city centre in the southeast will be off-limits to demonstrators this weekend, while in Paris protesters will only be allowed to march a limited route between Bastille and Nation squares. Authorities in Marseille had also banned protests but announced Friday that a union-organised demonstration would be allowed on an “exceptional basis” — the only one authorised in the southern Bouches-du-Rhone department. They also reversed a decision to suspend all public transport in the city on Saturday. But in the capital, leading museums including the Louvre will be closed on Saturday while the Art Basel art fair is being cut short. Some 20 percent more members of the security forces will be deployed this weekend after heavy criticism of the anticipation and intelligence gathering of police last week. “In a country governed by the rule of law, the police have a responsibility both to ensure that protests can take place peacefully and safely and to protect the public from violent disorder,” said Eva Cosse, senior Europe researcher at Human Rights Watch, expressing alarm over reports of children being severely injured by crowd-control weapons. The violence has tarnished the image of France ahead of elections that could be a turning point in its modern history, with the government’s debt pile also troubling investors. A new poll by Harris Interactive for M6/RTL made after the violence showed Le Pen soaring ahead on 33-35 percent in the first round of voting for the presidential elections. It predicted that hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon was on course to face her in the run-off where Le Pen would emerge as an easy winner on some 70 percent of the vote. item.title: One dead, three injured as two-storey building collapses in Lagos
item.description: ​By Olasunkanmi Akoni Tragedy struck in the early hours on Friday when one yet-to-be-identified construction worker was reportedly confirmed dead and three others critically injured following the midnight collapse of an uncomplicated two-storey building project in Lagos State. ​The unfortunate incident occurred along Akinola Street, near Fadeyi Bus Stop, off the busy Ikorodu Road axis. ​According to local sources, the victims were part of a crew that chose to sleep overnight at the site to prepare for an early start on the next day’s construction work. Reports said disaster struck in the middle of the night when the entire structure suddenly caved in, trapping the workers beneath the rubble. ​Emergency responders, led by the Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) alongside auxiliary safety teams, arrived at the scene shortly after the incident to commence search and rescue operations. First responders managed to pull three survivors from the debris with varying degrees of injury, while one body was recovered from the ruins. ​Meanwhile, the survivors have been rushed to a nearby hospital for medical treatment, while emergency crews continue to clear the site to ensure no additional victims remain trapped. ​Details surrounding the cause of the collapse remain sketchy as of press time. LASEMA Permanent Secretary, Dr. Femi Oke-Osanyintolu, who confirmed the incident said the cause of collapse cannot be ascertained presently. . “Emergency responders are making frantic efforts to ascertain the number of people (onsite workers) trapped beneath the collapsed structure. “Coordinated search and rescue ongoing with the agency’s excavator. “Meanwhile, ad at 3:33am, three adult ales rescued alive, while one ault male recovered dead. Operations ongoing,” Oke-Osanyintolu stated. The post One dead, three injured as two-storey building collapses in Lagos appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ex-agitator questions coastal highway re-routing
item.description: By Chancel Bomadi Sunday BOMADI — A Niger Delta ex-agitator and former Delta State House of Assembly candidate, Chief Kingsley Muturu, has called on the Federal Government to provide clear explanations for the proposed re-routing of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway to link with the existing East-West Road. Muturu, who contested under the All Progressives Congress (APC), said the proposed adjustment by the Minister of Works, David Umahi, had raised concerns in the Niger Delta, stressing the need for transparency regarding the reasons for the decision and its technical justification. Speaking with journalists over the weekend, the former agitator and peace ambassador said the government should explain the proposed changes, particularly in view of the survey plans and engineering designs already developed for the project. He argued that the region deserved clear information about the original highway alignment, the proposed adjustments and how the project would connect with the existing East-West Road. Muturu questioned whether the Niger Delta’s difficult terrain should pose an obstacle to the construction of major transport infrastructure, noting that the region had long supported petroleum exploration and transportation activities. “The Federal Government has demonstrated its capacity to construct major bridges and transport infrastructure across lagoons, rivers and other challenging waterways beyond the Niger Delta, which generates the nation’s wealth,” he said. “Why should the same terrain, which can be assessed and engineered for petroleum operations, automatically become an insurmountable obstacle to road construction?” He called for transparency and responsible leadership in decisions concerning the highway, warning against using the region’s geographical challenges as a reason to limit infrastructure development. Muturu noted that the oil industry had developed the technical capacity to explore, drill, install pipelines and transport crude oil across difficult terrain. He urged political leaders, traditional rulers and community stakeholders in the Niger Delta to demand fair treatment and equitable infrastructure development. The former lawmaker, however, acknowledged that oil exploration and road construction involved different engineering processes, technical requirements and environmental considerations. “Our point is straightforward: if the terrain can be studied and suitable engineering solutions devised for oil exploration and transportation, then the feasibility of roads, bridges and other essential infrastructure should likewise be evaluated through thorough technical investigations,” he said. “The Niger Delta deserves engineering solutions, not assumptions that its geography renders development impractical.” He maintained that a project of national significance such as the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway should be guided by credible technical evidence, transparent decision-making and meaningful engagement with communities that could

item.content:encoded: By Chancel Bomadi Sunday BOMADI — A Niger Delta ex-agitator and former Delta State House of Assembly candidate, Chief Kingsley Muturu, has called on the Federal Government to provide clear explanations for the proposed re-routing of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway to link with the existing East-West Road. Muturu, who contested under the All Progressives Congress (APC), said the proposed adjustment by the Minister of Works, David Umahi, had raised concerns in the Niger Delta, stressing the need for transparency regarding the reasons for the decision and its technical justification. Speaking with journalists over the weekend, the former agitator and peace ambassador said the government should explain the proposed changes, particularly in view of the survey plans and engineering designs already developed for the project. He argued that the region deserved clear information about the original highway alignment, the proposed adjustments and how the project would connect with the existing East-West Road. Muturu questioned whether the Niger Delta’s difficult terrain should pose an obstacle to the construction of major transport infrastructure, noting that the region had long supported petroleum exploration and transportation activities. “The Federal Government has demonstrated its capacity to construct major bridges and transport infrastructure across lagoons, rivers and other challenging waterways beyond the Niger Delta, which generates the nation’s wealth,” he said. “Why should the same terrain, which can be assessed and engineered for petroleum operations, automatically become an insurmountable obstacle to road construction?” He called for transparency and responsible leadership in decisions concerning the highway, warning against using the region’s geographical challenges as a reason to limit infrastructure development. Muturu noted that the oil industry had developed the technical capacity to explore, drill, install pipelines and transport crude oil across difficult terrain. He urged political leaders, traditional rulers and community stakeholders in the Niger Delta to demand fair treatment and equitable infrastructure development. The former lawmaker, however, acknowledged that oil exploration and road construction involved different engineering processes, technical requirements and environmental considerations. “Our point is straightforward: if the terrain can be studied and suitable engineering solutions devised for oil exploration and transportation, then the feasibility of roads, bridges and other essential infrastructure should likewise be evaluated through thorough technical investigations,” he said. “The Niger Delta deserves engineering solutions, not assumptions that its geography renders development impractical.” He maintained that a project of national significance such as the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway should be guided by credible technical evidence, transparent decision-making and meaningful engagement with communities that could be affected by changes to its alignment. Muturu urged President Bola Tinubu and the Federal Ministry of Works to ensure that decisions on the project were based on sound engineering principles, economic considerations, environmental protection and fairness to affected communities. item.title: What is The Hidden Cost of Nigerian Women’s Unpaid Labour?
item.description: Mother and children preparing food in a bright, cosy kitchen setting. Credit: RDNE Stock Project/Pexels. Fadekemi was six when she first felt the sting of splattered hot oil on her skin. She recalls her mother’s stern voice instructing her on how to make stew the way her father liked it. Fifty-one years and thousands of stew pots later, Fadekemi still wonders if that’s all she was made to do. In different parts of Nigeria today, there are millions of women like Fadekemi, each spending at least 5 hours daily on unpaid care and domestic work. Although Nigerians rarely pay women for care and domestic duties, research shows that it is real work with an annual economic value of up to $111 billion . How Women Carry Nigeria’s Unpaid Labour According to the Nigeria Time Use Survey (NTUS) 2024 report, the average Nigerian woman spends 21% of her day on unpaid domestic and care work ; this equals 5 extra hours, while men spend just one hour on unpaid work. This means that after spending 8 hours at work, she spends another 5 hours doing childcare and household work, making it a double shift. Yet when you look at the economic drivers of Nigeria’s economy, her time or work does not count; it is seen as a woman’s work. This inequality is seen as invisible labour. We see it show up in different phases of women’s lives, yet we still miss how heavy an unequal burden this is. Right from when a girl is 13, she becomes an unpaid labourer, doing domestic chores, taking care of siblings, yet these contributions are seen as nothing to Nigeria’s GDP. For Fadekemi, this unpaid labour started at six, continued into her teenage years, where she became a caregiver for her siblings, extended into motherhood, and now, as a grandmother, she continues to be a caregiver for her grandchildren because even traditions like Omugwo exclude men from care duties. Behind those hours of unpaid labour is a missed opportunity for the country’s GDP growth. What Happens When Care Is Shared? In a 2026 study published in BMC Paediatrics, over 64% of women said they were the primary caregivers of their newborn children. In some cases, this is a result of traditional belief systems that reinforce gender roles and assign domestic duties to women. In other cases, it is a systemic failure caused by policies that reinforce gender inequality. In Nigeria, for example, mothers are entitled to maternity leave with 50% pay, while only fathers in the civil service are entitled to 14 days of paternity leave. So what happens to private sector fathers? The national policy designs them to be absent fathers from day one and reinforces the narrative that their sole role is to be a provider and presence doesn’t matter. Experts have highlighted that cutting a new mother’s salary by 50% while excluding most fathers from paid leave reinforces the belief that a man’s primary duty is to be a financial provider and makes it harder for them to be present. And when that happens, care once again becomes the woman’s job.

And when that happens, care once again becomes the woman’s job. According to Nigeria’s proposed National Care Policy, when care duties are shared, the entire country benefits. Care moves from an unpaid, largely invisible responsibility to a thriving economic sector that creates jobs, supports businesses, strengthens national productivity, and enables millions of women to participate more fully in the labour market. Recognising the value of care work drives employment of 1.7 million mothers and could add $111 billion to the economy, 8 times more than the oil sector. This invisible labour has a price tag, and even though it appears that Nigerian women are the only ones who bear the cost, the entire country pays for it. When one segment of the population is unable to fully participate in the labour market, growth stalls for everyone. If you’d like to provide input on the draft of the National Care Policy, please do so at nigeriacarepolicy.org . item.title: PSG v Lyon French Ligue 1 game postponed due to Paris protests
item.description: PSG’s home Ligue 1 game against Lyon scheduled for this Sunday has been postponed until Monday, the French league announced, following a request by police amid a wave of violent protests in the French capital. “The LFP takes note of the police decree prohibiting the staging of the game between Paris Saint-Germain and Olympique Lyonnais on Sunday at 8:45 pm (1945 GMT)… and has decided to reschedule the match for Monday at 8:30 pm,” the French league said in a statement. French authorities are braced for another weekend of protests in Paris and across the country after some of the worst urban violence in years erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations a week ago. The post PSG v Lyon French Ligue 1 game postponed due to Paris protests appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FG Designates Redeemer’s Health Village As TETFund Centre, Guarantees Scholarships For Robotic Surgery Academy
item.description: In a breakthrough for Nigeria’s healthcare sector, the Federal Government has adopted the newly inaugurated Redeemer’s Health Village (RHV) Robotic Surgery Academy as the nation’s 29th TETFund Centre of Excellence, guaranteeing full scholarship coverage for all enrolled trainees. Speaking at the official inauguration on Thursday, Minister of Education Dr. Tunji Alausa declared that the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) will fully fund the tuition fees of qualified medical professionals undergoing specialist training at the academy through its local scholarship scheme. ﻿ The strategic partnership — established alongside RoboMed Global, the National Postgraduate Medical College of Nigeria (NPMCN), and Redeemer’s University — establishes Nigeria’s pioneer institute for advanced robotic and telesurgical operations. ₦250bn Healthcare Injection Highlighting the government’s drive to curb brain drain and eliminate foreign medical tourism, Alausa disclosed that the Federal Government has injected over ₦250 billion into medical education across the last two years. “The same number of medical students admitted while I was in medical school is the same number we have maintained over the years, without sufficient consideration of our population growth,” the minister stated, confirming plans to expand annual medical programme enrolments to 20,000 within two years. By designating RHV as a Special Centre of Excellence, TETFund sponsorship will ensure that financial barriers do not stop top clinical talent from acquiring cutting-edge surgical skills locally. $4m Infrastructure The newly launched academy hits the ground running with $4 million worth of dual robotic surgical systems, designed to power both clinical service delivery and high-level training. According to RHV Chief Executive Officer Adedamola Dada, the academy aims to produce 400 certified specialists within two years across three main specialties: Urology, General Surgery, and Gynaecology. The academy’s scope extends beyond doctors to train an entire technical ecosystem, including operating theatre personnel, biomedical engineers, and hospital administrators. RHV also recently achieved full accreditation as an academic medical school. Co-founder of RoboMed Global, Dr. Obi Ekwenna, emphasised that the academy relies on a total-ecosystem training model inspired by aviation safety standards prioritizing communication, simulation, and strict team coordination. “The essence of the academy is to train the entire ecosystem, not just surgeons alone,” Ekwenna noted, explaining that candidate evaluation will blend advanced simulation, supervised clinical practice, and structured patient care. Institutional Backing, Local Accreditation The National Postgraduate Medical College of Nigeria (NPMCN) will oversee the academic standards and award official postgraduate fellowship diplomas upon completion, while Redeemer’s University will lead specialised training for nursing teams and biomedical maintenance eng

Speaking at the official inauguration on Thursday, Minister of Education Dr. Tunji Alausa declared that the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) will fully fund the tuition fees of qualified medical professionals undergoing specialist training at the academy through its local scholarship scheme. ﻿ The strategic partnership — established alongside RoboMed Global, the National Postgraduate Medical College of Nigeria (NPMCN), and Redeemer’s University — establishes Nigeria’s pioneer institute for advanced robotic and telesurgical operations. ₦250bn Healthcare Injection Highlighting the government’s drive to curb brain drain and eliminate foreign medical tourism, Alausa disclosed that the Federal Government has injected over ₦250 billion into medical education across the last two years. “The same number of medical students admitted while I was in medical school is the same number we have maintained over the years, without sufficient consideration of our population growth,” the minister stated, confirming plans to expand annual medical programme enrolments to 20,000 within two years. By designating RHV as a Special Centre of Excellence, TETFund sponsorship will ensure that financial barriers do not stop top clinical talent from acquiring cutting-edge surgical skills locally. $4m Infrastructure The newly launched academy hits the ground running with $4 million worth of dual robotic surgical systems, designed to power both clinical service delivery and high-level training. According to RHV Chief Executive Officer Adedamola Dada, the academy aims to produce 400 certified specialists within two years across three main specialties: Urology, General Surgery, and Gynaecology. The academy’s scope extends beyond doctors to train an entire technical ecosystem, including operating theatre personnel, biomedical engineers, and hospital administrators. RHV also recently achieved full accreditation as an academic medical school. Co-founder of RoboMed Global, Dr. Obi Ekwenna, emphasised that the academy relies on a total-ecosystem training model inspired by aviation safety standards prioritizing communication, simulation, and strict team coordination. “The essence of the academy is to train the entire ecosystem, not just surgeons alone,” Ekwenna noted, explaining that candidate evaluation will blend advanced simulation, supervised clinical practice, and structured patient care. Institutional Backing, Local Accreditation The National Postgraduate Medical College of Nigeria (NPMCN) will oversee the academic standards and award official postgraduate fellowship diplomas upon completion, while Redeemer’s University will lead specialised training for nursing teams and biomedical maintenance engineers. Vice-Chancellor of Redeemer’s University, Prof. Shadrach Akindele, and NPMCN President Prof. Anthony Ikefuna both hailed the project as a decisive milestone. Following RHV’s landmark execution of Nigeria’s first robotic and telesurgical procedures in September, the academy is positioned to establish West Africa as a regional hub for technology-driven patient care. Redeemer’s Health Village is a faith-based tertiary medical facility established by the Redeemed Christian Church of God (RCCG). item.title: Jide Kosoko laments debt as N300m cinema film fails to make profit
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Veteran Nollywood actor and filmmaker Jide Kosoko says he is in debt after his film, Eleko: Oba Esugbayi , failed to recoup its production cost of more than N300 million at the cinemas. Kosoko made the disclosure in a recent interview with African A-List, saying the film was financed by investors who expected returns, not money given to him as a gift. “My film ‘Eleko: Oba Esugbayi’ that recently came out and we took to the cinemas, cost us over N300 million. Do I have 300 million? You should know that some people gave it to me and it was not that they dashed me; they invested in it and we took the film to the cinemas,” he said. The filmmaker said the movie did not generate enough revenue to recover the investment. The small amount it earned was shared among those involved in the project. “Different things happened and we did not earn our money back. The little that was earned was split. As I am, if you hear someone with debt dancing around their neck, it is me,” Kosoko said. In another account of the interview, Kosoko was quoted as clarifying that the debt remark was not necessarily a reference to unpaid wages. He said the people who worked on the production had been paid, but the film did not deliver the financial returns he and the investors had hoped for. He also acknowledged the substantial investments made by cinema operators when asked about the film’s cinema earnings and their distribution. “I won’t deceive anyone, but truly, those who own the cinemas have huge investments,” he said. Kosoko’s comments echo concerns raised by actor and filmmaker Ramsey Nouah, who has said that releasing a film in cinemas does not always make financial sense. Nouah said only a small fraction of cinema releases recover their production costs and turn a profit, adding that producers can still fail to recoup their investment after spending heavily on advertising and promotion. The post Jide Kosoko laments debt as N300m cinema film fails to make profit appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Casualties feared as multi-storey building collapses in Nairobi
item.description: A multi-storey building collapsed mid-construction in the Kenyan capital on Friday, the Red Cross said, with reports from local media of casualties and looting at the site. Videos spreading online showed a dramatic crash and huge clouds of dust as the building came down in a busy business and residential district. “At around 1340 hours, a multi-storey building under construction collapsed on 9th Street in Eastleigh, Nairobi,” the Red Cross posted on X, adding that it had dispatched a team. Local media reported looting and possible casualties trapped beneath the rubble, with images showing large crowds gathered at the site. There were conflicting reports on the size of the building, which may have been as high as 18 storeys. Eastleigh is a densely packed residential and market area, known as a hub for the Somali community. Nairobi is undergoing an extremely rapid construction boom, with high-rise buildings appearing all over the city as Kenya’s population expands. AFP The post Casualties feared as multi-storey building collapses in Nairobi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: UK urges households to stockpile essentials for emergencies
item.description: Bottled water: check. Torch: check. Blankets: check. UK leader Andy Burnham said Britons need to be better prepared for emergencies on Friday, when he hosted a wildfire and resilience summit. The prime minister highlighted a new government campaign that urges households to stockpile essential items in case everyday services are disrupted by anything from severe weather to cyberattacks. The “Be Ready” initiative advises storing three days’ worth of bottled water and non-perishable food, a battery or wind-up FM radio to receive updates during outages, and banknotes and coins in case electronic payments or cash machines are disrupted. Sleeping bags, spare batteries and toiletries are also on the checklist, which was published on Thursday and is in line with guidance issued in France, Ireland and The Netherlands. “We’re having the conversation with people about being better prepared because we’re living in a world where unexpected events seem to be becoming more and more common,” said Burnham, giving storms as an example. “It is just having those supplies in the house to get you through those moments. So we are having that conversation about resilience.” Burnham was speaking after he told a meeting of fire chiefs, local leaders and experts in Liverpool, northwest England, that UK military helicopters and planes would be equipped to fight wildfires. English firefighting services will also get additional specialist wildfire teams and lightweight personal protective equipment, with the government saying it was earmarking up to £45 million ($60 million) to counter the increase in blazes. The UK has faced widespread droughts, extreme heat and resulting wildfires each summer in recent years, in a trend scientists have blamed on man-made climate change. One blaze in Stourbridge, central England, in August gutted 19 houses and damaged 18 others, prompting Burnham to warn on a visit there that Britain must face up to the changing climate and accelerate its transition to clean energy. The UK leader was criticised by environmental campaigners this week after approving plans to start new drilling within a controversial North Sea gas field. Regarding the “Be Ready” campaign, which will last three years, Defence Minister Wes Streeting told the BBC late on Thursday that the government wanted “people to be alert but not alarmed”. Earlier, he said households and businesses need to ask themselves whether they are prepared if there is “disruption to essential supply chains caused by hostile state actors or terrorists”. “How would we cope if the payment systems at the local supermarket went down?” he asked. Concerns about food security were raised this month when major French supermarket chains were hit by a cyberattack that caused their refrigerators to shoot up in temperature in hundreds of stores, forcing spoilt food to be thrown away. item.title: Nigerian man dies in sleep in UK; leaves wife, two children
item.description: The Nigerian Community in the United Kingdom has announced the death of a Nigerian man, Ekeobong Omega Nelson, who died at the age of 35, leaving behind his wife and two young children. The community announced his death in a statement shared on its X account on Friday, October 23, saying Nelson died on October 17, 2026. THE NIGERIAN COMMUNITY IN THE UK ANNOUNCES WITH DEEP SADNESS IN LOVING MEMORY OF OUR DEAR BROTHER EKEOBONG OMEGA NELSON It is with profound sadness and heavy hearts that we announce the passing of our dear friend and brother, Ekeobong Omega Nelson, who passed away on 17th… pic.twitter.com/vs3lZdWPh2 — Nigerian Community UK (@NCUKCommunity) October 23, 2026 According to the statement, his death came as a shock to his family, friends and members of the Nigerian community because he was not known to be ill. “His passing came as a devastating shock to everyone, as he was not known to be ill. He went to sleep and sadly did not wake up,” the statement read. The community described Nelson’s death as a painful loss. It called on well-wishers to offer prayers, love and comfort to the family as they cope with the loss. The statement concluded with a prayer for strength for Nelson’s wife and children and for the deceased to rest in peace. Vanguard News The post Nigerian man dies in sleep in UK; leaves wife, two children appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Indonesia’s Haze Crisis Raises Accountability Demands On Corporate Firms
item.description: After months of fires in Indonesia that have caused thick regional haze, attention is turning to whether companies can be held accountable for the blazes and resulting air pollution. Indonesia regularly experiences fires during its dry season, and experts say years of deforestation and peatland drainage for cultivation have left previously fire-resistant landscapes vulnerable. Driven by a strong El Nino cycle and resulting drought, this year’s blazes have been particularly severe, burning through nearly two million hectares, according to deforestation monitor Nusantara Atlas. The fires have raged across forests and peatland but also palm oil and timber plantations supplying multinational firms. Environmental group WALHI says it mapped “high confidence” hotspots across Indonesia using NASA fire data and found around 50 percent were inside concessions. In a report this month the group listed 40 timber and palm oil concessions by the number of hotspots detected. “This is a structural issue… (that) happens because of the practices, the activities, of these companies,” WALHI forests and plantations campaigner Umi Ma’rufah told AFP. Civil society groups have regularly accused companies of responsibility for the blazes, pointing to so-called “hotspots” in supplier plantations, sometimes called concessions. Demonstrators wearing gas masks hold protest placards outside China’s embassy to demand an audit of supply chains linked to Indonesian forest fires, in Jakarta on October 22, 2026. (Photo by BAY ISMOYO / AFP) Pressure is also coming from governments, including Singapore, which has issued 10 companies with “preventative measure notices” under its Transboundary Haze Pollution Act. The notices urge them to fight fires on their land, prevent burning and submit action plans. Firms can face legal action including fines if they do not comply. “We must also be clear about where the responsibility for this lies,” Singapore Senior Minister K. Shanmugam told reporters. “This was not simply an act of nature, but a problem driven by companies pursuing profits.” Legal liability Several companies implicated have insisted they are not behind the fires. “Fires originating outside our boundaries subsequently spread into areas under the Group’s management,” Singapore Exchange-listed palm oil company First Resources said after one of its concessions was listed in WALHI’s report. Asia Pulp and Paper, a Singapore-registered firm, also insisted that fires in supplier concessions do not “necessarily mean that land was deliberately burned or that the concession holder was responsible for starting the fire.” Satellite monitoring can sometimes show where fires started, said Nusantara Atlas founder David Gaveau. “In some cases, the satellite photos clearly show that fire starts inside, but we cannot say whether it’s by design or whether it’s accidental,” he told AFP. “In other cases it’s also clear that fire started outside and spread inside the concession.” Experts say fire has
item.dc:creator: Khadijat Lawal
item.content:encoded: After months of fires in Indonesia that have caused thick regional haze, attention is turning to whether companies can be held accountable for the blazes and resulting air pollution. Indonesia regularly experiences fires during its dry season, and experts say years of deforestation and peatland drainage for cultivation have left previously fire-resistant landscapes vulnerable. Driven by a strong El Nino cycle and resulting drought, this year’s blazes have been particularly severe, burning through nearly two million hectares, according to deforestation monitor Nusantara Atlas. The fires have raged across forests and peatland but also palm oil and timber plantations supplying multinational firms. Environmental group WALHI says it mapped “high confidence” hotspots across Indonesia using NASA fire data and found around 50 percent were inside concessions. In a report this month the group listed 40 timber and palm oil concessions by the number of hotspots detected. “This is a structural issue… (that) happens because of the practices, the activities, of these companies,” WALHI forests and plantations campaigner Umi Ma’rufah told AFP. Civil society groups have regularly accused companies of responsibility for the blazes, pointing to so-called “hotspots” in supplier plantations, sometimes called concessions. Demonstrators wearing gas masks hold protest placards outside China’s embassy to demand an audit of supply chains linked to Indonesian forest fires, in Jakarta on October 22, 2026. (Photo by BAY ISMOYO / AFP) Pressure is also coming from governments, including Singapore, which has issued 10 companies with “preventative measure notices” under its Transboundary Haze Pollution Act. The notices urge them to fight fires on their land, prevent burning and submit action plans. Firms can face legal action including fines if they do not comply. “We must also be clear about where the responsibility for this lies,” Singapore Senior Minister K. Shanmugam told reporters. “This was not simply an act of nature, but a problem driven by companies pursuing profits.” Legal liability Several companies implicated have insisted they are not behind the fires. “Fires originating outside our boundaries subsequently spread into areas under the Group’s management,” Singapore Exchange-listed palm oil company First Resources said after one of its concessions was listed in WALHI’s report. Asia Pulp and Paper, a Singapore-registered firm, also insisted that fires in supplier concessions do not “necessarily mean that land was deliberately burned or that the concession holder was responsible for starting the fire.” Satellite monitoring can sometimes show where fires started, said Nusantara Atlas founder David Gaveau. “In some cases, the satellite photos clearly show that fire starts inside, but we cannot say whether it’s by design or whether it’s accidental,” he told AFP. “In other cases it’s also clear that fire started outside and spread inside the concession.” Experts say fire has been used in the past to illegally open up land for cultivation, including in large concessions, but also by smaller-scale local investors. Parts of Indonesia also previously allowed smallholders to use fire to clear plots of land, though this year the government has cracked down on that practice too. Even if fires begin accidentally or outside concessions, firms may have legal responsibilities, explained Azam Hawari, a lawyer with environmental law NGO ClientEarth. “An external source of ignition or extreme weather does not necessarily absolve a company of civil liability,” said Hawari. Companies are required to have sufficient fire measures, including personnel and equipment, and could also be liable “where activities pose a serious threat to the environment,” like peatland drainage, he added. International links Indonesia has announced “administrative sanctions” against dozens of firms and criminal proceedings against 125 individuals and corporations. But campaigner Umi pointed out that some previously prosecuted firms have failed to pay fines or carry out forest restoration. “It’s about the will from the government to really do their (enforcement) task,” she said. Some implicated concessions have ties well behind Indonesia’s borders, said Holly Yang, an accounting professor at Singapore Management University who teaches sustainability reporting. After WALHI’s report, she and her student Ashmit Bansal mapped concession holders, owners, creditors, investors and supply-chain partners. “The fires occur in Indonesia, but the ownership, financing and commercial relationships extend across borders,” Yang told AFP. Yang noted that a connection “does not, by itself, establish responsibility for a fire”. But mapping relationships “allows the public to ask informed questions and assess how those parties respond”. item.title: Retro gaming is being overrun with AI
item.description: Retro video games are everywhere lately - especially in places where they aren't supposed to be. Halo in a web browser , Wind Waker on the iPhone , Super Smash Bros. in mixed reality . Over the past month or so, these kinds of unexpected projects have gone viral with incredible frequency thanks to new AI tools, as hobbyists take apart games and then rebuild them for new platforms. But while AI has supercharged the pace of these ports, it's also tearing apart tight-knit communities dedicated to preserving games. item.title: 'Stupendously large black holes' aren't a major component of dark matter, study finds
item.description: null Black holes more massive than entire galaxies are not a major component of the mysterious dark matter that's thought to make up most of the matter in the cosmos, a new study finds. For decades, to explain why galaxies do not spin apart at the speeds at which they whirl, scientists have suggested the existence of an unseen substance known as dark matter , whose gravitational pull helps keep galaxies together. Dark matter is thought to make up about five-sixths of all matter in the universe . Much remains unknown about dark matter, however — including whether or not it actually exists. Black holes make good potential contenders for dark matter, since they are extremely massive and are difficult to spot in the dark depths of space. In the new study, researchers investigated whether dark matter could be made of " stupendously large black holes ," ones with masses greater than 100 billion times the mass of the sun . Stupendously large black holes greater than 1 million billion to 10 million billion suns in mass would be heavier than entire galaxies. So far, astronomers have not detected any stupendously large black holes — currently, the largest black hole known may weigh about 36 billion suns . Since researchers have not seen any even after looking at many galaxies, the new study noted they cannot make up all of dark matter — but team members wondered if the exotic objects still might constitute a significant portion of the puzzling substance. Often, dark matter is thought of "as a fine dust spread everywhere," study co-author Christopher Gerlach, a theoretical physicist at the Mainz Institute for Theoretical Physics in Germany, told Space.com. However, if dark matter is packed into a handful of gigantic objects such as stupendously large black holes, "the universe becomes grainy on very large scales. And we can check that." Specifically, the scientists analyzed the light from the dawn of the universe, study co-author Yann Gouttenoire, a theoretical physicist at the Mainz Institute for Theoretical Physics, told Space.com. For the first 380,000 years after the Big Bang , the cosmos was filled with a hot plasma in which light was trapped. Eventually, the expansion of the universe let the cosmos cool enough for the plasma to largely dissipate and form atoms. This in turn let light shine freely, "and that light is still arriving today," Gerlach explained. "We call it the cosmic microwave background , a snapshot of the infant universe covering the whole sky." The temperature of the cosmic microwave background "varies from place to place by about one part in 100,000," study co-author Antonio Iovino, a theoretical physicist at New York University, Abu Dhabi, in the United Arab Emirates, told Space.com. "That pattern tells us how matter was spread back then." An illustration of a supermassive black hole against a background of dark matter. (Image credit: Robert Lea (created with Canva)) Analyzing the cosmic microwave background revealed it is not grainy
